24382.q: What is a Roman farming estate called in Latin?
24382.e: “Villa rustica” means “country house”. There were many such estates in Switzerland.
24382.m: A farming estate is called a villa rustica in Latin.

24383.q: How were rich Roman country houses heated in winter?
a: With warm air under the floor
With hot stones in the bed
24383.e: Hot air from the fire flowed under the floor and through the walls. This heating is called a hypocaust.
24383.m: The Romans already had underfloor heating.

24384.q: Which Roman estate in the canton of Zurich is well known?
24384.e: The Seeb estate is near Winkel in the Zurich Unterland. You can visit the walls and a small museum.
24384.m: A Roman estate stood at Seeb.

24385.q: What is the Roman estate of Orbe-Boscéaz famous for?
24385.e: At Orbe in the canton of Vaud you can see splendid floor pictures. They show gods and animals, for example.
24385.m: There are beautiful Roman mosaics at Orbe.

24386.q: What is a Roman mosaic made of?
24386.e: A mosaic is put together from lots of tiny coloured stones. This makes a picture on the floor.
24386.m: A mosaic is made of tiny stones.

24387.q: Where did the owner of a Roman estate live?
24387.e: The owner lived in the fine main house with a bath and heating. Workers and animals lived in other buildings.
24387.m: The owner lived in the main house.

24388.q: Which plant did the Romans spread in Switzerland for a drink?
24388.e: The Romans liked drinking wine and planted vines. Coffee, tea and cocoa only came to Europe much later.

24389.q: In which canton is the Julier Pass, which the Romans already used?
24389.e: The Julier Pass is in the Grisons and is 2284 metres high. It links the Oberhalbstein with the Engadine.
24389.m: The Julier Pass is in the Grisons.

24390.q: What can still be seen at the top of the Julier Pass today?
24390.e: Remains of columns stand next to the pass road. They belonged to a Roman shrine.
24390.m: Remains of Roman columns stand on the Julier Pass.

24391.q: Which areas does the Great St Bernard Pass link?
24391.e: The pass leads from Valais into the Aosta Valley in Italy. For the Romans it was an important route to Gaul.
24391.m: The Great St Bernard links Valais with Italy.

24392.q: Which god was a temple on the Great St Bernard dedicated to?
24392.e: The Celts worshipped the god Poeninus there. The Romans equated him with Jupiter.
24392.m: A temple to Jupiter stood on the Great St Bernard.

24393.q: Roughly how high is the Great St Bernard Pass?
24393.e: The pass is 2469 metres above sea level. In winter it is closed for a long time because of snow.
24393.m: The Great St Bernard is almost 2500 metres high.

24394.q: What did the milestones on Roman roads show?
24394.e: Milestones were stone columns at the side of the road. They said how far it was to a certain town.

24395.q: How did people travel on Roman roads?
a: On foot, on horseback or by cart
24395.e: The Romans walked, rode or travelled by cart. They did not need elephants and camels for this.
24395.m: On Roman roads people travelled on foot, on horseback or by cart.

24396.q: Why did the Romans build good roads over the Alps?
a: So that soldiers and traders could travel fast
So that herders could take their herds up to the alpine pastures
So that mountain farmers could bring wood down to the valley
So that gladiators could get to Rome
24396.e: On good roads soldiers and goods moved faster. That way the Romans could hold their great empire together.
24396.m: The Romans built roads for soldiers and trade.

24397.e: The name Zurich developed from the old name Turicum. Turicum was a small Roman settlement.

24398.q: What was there in the Roman settlement of Turicum?
24398.e: In Turicum traders had to pay customs duty on their goods. A border between two Roman provinces ran here.
24398.m: People paid customs duty in Turicum.

24399.q: On which hill in Zurich did a Roman fort stand?
24399.e: On the Lindenhof the Romans built a fortress with ten towers. Today there is a square with trees there.
24399.m: A Roman fort stood on the Lindenhof.

24400.q: Where was the name Turicum found for the first time?
24400.e: In 1747 a gravestone for a small child was found. The child’s father was the head of the customs post.
24400.m: A gravestone is the first to mention the name Turicum.

24401.e: Turicum lay where the Limmat flows out of Lake Zurich. Goods could easily be reloaded there.

24402.q: What from Roman times was found near the Weinplatz in Zurich?
24402.e: In the Thermengasse near the Weinplatz, remains of Roman baths were discovered in 1983. The lane is named after these baths.
24402.m: A Roman bath stood near the Weinplatz in Zurich.

24404.q: Who was the Roman fort in Zurich meant to protect against?
24404.e: In the 4th century the Alemanni attacked the Roman Empire. That is why the Romans built strong walls around their towns.
24404.m: The fort in Zurich protected against the Alemanni.

24405.q: Which town was called Lousonna in Roman times?
24405.e: Lousonna was a Roman settlement on the lakeshore. Lausanne later developed from it.

24406.e: Lousonna lay right on the shore of Lake Geneva. It had a harbour there.

24407.q: Which present-day Swiss city was called Lousonna in Roman times?
24407.e: The Roman settlement of Lousonna lay on Lake Geneva in what is now the Vidy district of Lausanne. There is a Roman museum there.

24408.q: Which well-known organisation has its headquarters today where Lousonna once was?
24408.e: The headquarters of the Olympic Committee stands in Vidy. Remains of the Roman settlement lie underneath and beside it.
24408.m: The Olympic Committee is now based where Lousonna lay.

24409.q: How did the Romans in Lousonna move heavy goods across Lake Geneva?
a: With pack animals along the shore
24409.e: An inscription by boatmen shows that there was shipping on the lake. Heavy goods travelled well on the water.
24409.m: The Romans transported goods across the lake by ship.

24410.q: Which people lived in Genava when the Romans came?
24410.e: At that time Celtic tribes lived in the area around Genava. The Romans called the region Gaul.

24411.q: Which river flows out of the lake in Geneva?
24411.e: In Geneva the Rhône leaves the lake. It then flows on into France.
24411.m: In Geneva the Rhône flows out of the lake.

24412.q: What did Caesar have destroyed in Genava in 58 BC to stop the Helvetii?
24412.e: Without a bridge the Helvetii could not easily cross the river. That way Caesar blocked their path.
24412.m: Caesar had the bridge in Genava destroyed.

24413.q: In which famous book is Genava first mentioned?
24413.e: Julius Caesar described his wars in Gaul in a book. In it he also mentions Genava.
24413.m: Genava appears in Caesar’s book about the Gallic War.

24414.q: Which present-day town did the Romans call Vitudurum?
24414.e: Vitudurum was a Roman settlement in the district of Oberwinterthur. It later became Winterthur.

24415.q: Which present-day town did the Romans call Salodurum?
24415.e: Salodurum lay on the Aare. Over time the name became Solothurn.

24416.q: Which present-day town did the Romans call Curia?
24416.e: Curia was a Roman town in Raetia. Today Chur is the capital of the Grisons.

24417.q: Which present-day city did the Romans call Basilia?
24417.e: Basilia lay on the Rhine on the Minster hill. The name Basel came from it.

24418.q: Which people do many place names ending in “-dunum” and “-durum”, such as Eburodunum or Salodurum, come from?
24418.e: The Celts lived in the area of Switzerland before the Romans. The Romans took over many Celtic place names, for example Salodurum for Solothurn.
24418.m: Place names ending in -dunum and -durum are Celtic.

24419.q: Which present-day town did the Romans call Aquae Helveticae?
24419.e: “Aquae” means “waters”. Baden has warm springs where even the Romans bathed.

24420.q: Which present-day town on Lake Constance did the Romans call Arbor Felix?
24420.e: Arbor Felix means “happy tree”. The name later became Arbon.

24421.q: Which present-day town on Lake Geneva did the Romans call Noviodunum?
24421.e: Noviodunum was a Celtic name. The Romans founded a colony there, which became Nyon.

24422.q: Which present-day town did the Romans call Eburodunum?
24422.e: Eburodunum lay at the southern end of Lake Neuchâtel. Today the town is called Yverdon-les-Bains.

24423.q: Which present-day place is where the Roman town of Augusta Raurica was?
24423.e: Augusta Raurica was a large Roman town on the Rhine near Basel. Today the villages of Augst and Kaiseraugst are there.
24423.m: Augusta Raurica was at present-day Augst.

24424.q: What do you call a boy who begins his training as a knight in a castle at about 7 years old?
24424.e: Training to be a knight usually began at about 7, as a page. The page lived at a lord’s court and served him.
24424.m: At about 7, a boy became a page.

24425.q: What is a young man called who serves a knight and wants to become a knight himself?
24425.e: The squire helped a knight and learned fighting from him. Later he could become a knight himself.
24425.m: A squire serves a knight and learns from him.

24426.q: At about what age did a page become a squire?
24426.e: At about 14, a page was solemnly made a squire. Then his training with weapons began.
24426.m: At about 14, a page became a squire.

24427.q: What did a page learn first at court?
24427.e: A page served at table and learned how to behave properly at court. He also had his first riding lessons.
24427.m: A page first learned good manners at court.

24428.q: What did a squire help his knight with before a fight?
24428.e: It was almost impossible to put on armour by yourself. The squire helped the knight with it and also looked after his weapons.
24428.m: The squire helped the knight into his armour.

24429.q: Which of the knight’s animals did a squire have to look after?
24429.e: The squire made sure his knight’s horse was cared for. In battle he often also led a spare horse.
24429.m: A squire looked after his knight’s horse.

24430.q: What did a squire hand his knight at a tournament when his lance had broken?
24430.e: At tournaments and in battle, the squire brought the knight new weapons. Lances in particular often broke.
24430.m: The squire brought his knight new weapons.

24433.q: With what did the lord touch the squire’s shoulder when knighting him?
24433.e: The lord laid the flat side of his sword on the squire’s shoulder. That was the sign of knighting.
24433.m: When someone is knighted, a sword touches their shoulder.

24434.q: At about what age was a squire knighted?
24434.e: A squire could become a knight at about 21. Before that he had to prove his courage and loyalty.
24434.m: At about 21, a squire could become a knight.

24435.q: What did the squire do in front of his lord when he was knighted?
24435.e: The squire knelt down in front of his lord. That was how he showed his respect.
24435.m: When being knighted, the squire kneels down.

24436.q: What did a new knight promise his lord?
24436.e: The new knight swore to serve his lord loyally. Loyalty was very important for knights.
24436.m: A knight promised his lord loyalty.

24437.e: Only someone who was a knight himself, or a great lord such as a king, was allowed to knight someone.
24437.m: Only a knight or a ruler could knight someone.

24438.q: Who still knights people in Great Britain today?
24438.e: In Great Britain the King, as of 2026 King Charles III, knights people who deserve it. Today it is an honour for special achievements.
24438.m: Knighthoods still exist in Great Britain today.

24439.q: Which title does a man in Great Britain receive when he is knighted?
24439.e: A man who is knighted in Great Britain is called “Sir” afterwards. One example is the musician Sir Paul McCartney.
24439.m: A British knight is addressed as Sir.

24440.q: What is a coat of arms?
24440.e: A coat of arms is a coloured emblem. It belongs to a family, a town or a country.
24440.m: A coat of arms is a coloured sign of recognition.

24441.q: Why did knights paint a coat of arms on their shield?
a: So that people could recognise them
So that the shield brought luck
24441.e: In armour and with a helmet, one knight looked just like another. You could recognise him by the coat of arms on his shield.
24441.m: You recognised a knight in armour by his coat of arms.

24442.q: What does the Swiss coat of arms show?
24442.e: The Swiss coat of arms shows a white cross on a red background. You see the same emblem on the Swiss flag.
24442.m: The Swiss coat of arms has a white cross on red.

24443.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of Bern?
24443.e: A black bear walks across the coat of arms of Bern. The bear is the heraldic animal of the city and canton of Bern.
24443.m: The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern.

24444.q: What does the coat of arms of the canton of Uri show?
24444.e: The coat of arms of Uri shows a black bull’s head on a yellow background. It is called the Uri bull.
24444.m: There is a bull’s head on the coat of arms of Uri.

24445.q: Which animal appears most often on coats of arms?
24445.e: The lion is the most common heraldic animal. It stands for courage and strength.
24445.m: The lion is the most common animal on coats of arms.

24446.q: What does the coat of arms of the canton of Basel-Stadt show?
24446.e: The coat of arms of Basel-Stadt shows a black Basel crozier on white. The staff is a reminder of the Bishop of Basel.
24446.m: Basel-Stadt has a black Basel crozier on its coat of arms.

24447.q: What shape is a coat of arms usually?
24447.e: Coats of arms began on the shields of knights. That is why they still usually have the shape of a shield today.
24447.m: A coat of arms usually has the shape of a shield.

24449.q: At a tournament, what did two knights use to try to knock each other off their horses?
24449.e: Two knights rode towards each other. With their long lances they tried to hit their opponent or lift him out of the saddle.
24449.m: At tournaments, knights fought with lances.

24450.q: Why did tournament lances often have a blunt tip?
a: So that nobody got badly hurt
So that they could be thrown
24450.e: Nobody was supposed to be killed at a tournament. That is why the lances were often blunt, but there were still injuries.
24450.m: Tournament lances were blunt so that nobody got badly hurt.

24451.q: In later jousting, what separated the two riders?
24451.e: Later a wooden barrier was put up between the riders. That way the horses could not crash into each other.
24451.m: A wooden barrier separated the riders when jousting.

24452.q: What did a defeated knight often have to give the winner at a tournament?
24452.e: A defeated knight often had to hand over his horse and armour to the winner. He could also buy them back with money.
24452.m: Whoever lost a tournament often had to give up his horse and armour.

24453.q: What else were tournaments useful for to knights?
24453.e: At tournaments, knights practised fighting on horseback. That way they were prepared for war.
24453.m: At tournaments, knights practised for war.

24454.q: What did a knight sometimes receive from a lady before competing in a tournament?
24454.e: A lady sometimes gave a knight a cloth or a sleeve. The knight wore it at the tournament as a sign of her favour.
24454.m: At tournaments, a knight sometimes wore his lady’s cloth.

24455.q: What do you call a tournament fight in which many knights fight each other in groups?
24455.e: In a melee, two groups of riders charged at each other. They usually fought with blunt weapons.
24455.m: In a melee, groups of knights fought against each other.

24456.q: What is chain mail made of?
24456.e: Chain mail is made of thousands of small iron rings. Each ring is linked to several others.
24456.m: Chain mail is made of lots of small iron rings.

24457.q: What did a knight wear under his chain mail?
24457.e: Under the chain mail, people wore a thickly padded shirt. It softened blows and protected the skin from the rings.
24457.m: A padded shirt was worn under chain mail.

24458.q: What did chain mail protect especially well against?
24458.e: The iron rings kept out the edge of a sword well. Against hard blows, it was mainly the padding underneath that helped.

24459.q: Roughly how heavy was a shirt of chain mail?
24459.e: A simple shirt of chain mail with short sleeves weighed about 15 kilograms. The weight was spread over the whole body.
24459.m: A shirt of chain mail weighed about 15 kilograms.

24460.q: What is the later armour made of large metal plates called?
24460.e: In the late Middle Ages, knights wore armour made of large steel plates. It is called plate armour.
24460.m: Later, knights wore plate armour made of metal.

24461.q: What protected a knight’s head in battle?
24461.e: Knights wore a metal helmet. It protected the head from sword blows.
24461.m: The helmet protected the knight’s head.

24462.q: Why did a great helm have narrow slits at the front?
a: To tie it to the saddle
24462.e: Through the narrow eye slits the knight could look out. Small holes helped with breathing.
24462.m: The knight could see through the slits in his helmet.

24463.q: What is the part of a helmet that you can flip up in front of your face called?
24463.e: The visor protects the face. You can flip it up to see and breathe better.
24463.m: The visor is the hinged face guard on a helmet.

24464.q: On an early knight’s helmet, what protected the nose?
24464.e: Early helmets had a strip of metal at the front over the nose. It is called a nasal.
24464.m: A strip of metal on the helmet protected the nose.

24465.q: What do you call the strong horse a knight rode into battle?
24465.e: The warhorse was a strong, well-trained fighting horse. It had to be able to carry a knight in armour.
24465.m: A knight rode into battle on a warhorse.

24466.q: How expensive was a good warhorse?
a: As expensive as a loaf of bread
24466.e: A good warhorse cost a lot of money. Only rich people could afford such a horse.

24467.q: Were warhorses mostly stallions or mares?
24467.e: Stallions were usually chosen as warhorses. They were seen as strong and brave.

24468.q: What did a knight use at his heels to urge his horse on?
24468.e: Spurs are small metal parts on the boots. With them, the knight gave signals to the horse.
24468.m: A knight urged his horse on with spurs.

24469.q: What helped a knight stay firmly on his horse when striking with his lance?
24469.e: The knight could brace his feet firmly in the stirrups. That made him less likely to fall off when striking with the lance.
24469.m: The stirrups gave the knight a firm hold.

24470.q: What did a warhorse have to learn in training?
a: To stay calm in the noise of battle
24470.e: A warhorse must not run away in noise and chaos. That is why it was trained for a long time.
24470.m: A warhorse learned to stay calm in the noise.

24471.q: What did a warhorse sometimes wear for protection?
24471.e: Some warhorses wore armour made of metal or leather. It mainly protected the head and chest.

24472.q: What did a horse often wear that showed the knight’s coat of arms?
24472.e: A colourful cloth with the coat of arms was often laid over the horse. That way you could recognise the knight from far away.
24472.m: The horse’s covering often showed the knight’s coat of arms.

24473.q: Why did a knight often ride a different horse from his warhorse when travelling?
a: Because the warhorse was too small
24473.e: The valuable warhorse was meant to be rested for battle. So on journeys, the knight rode another horse.
24473.m: The warhorse was spared for battle.

24474.e: A virtue is a good quality in a person. Knights were supposed to have many virtues.
24474.m: A virtue is a good quality.

24475.q: What did the virtue of “loyalty” mean for a knight?
24475.e: Loyalty meant always staying true to your lord and to your word. A loyal knight did not let his lord down.
24475.m: Loyalty means standing by your lord.

24476.q: Whom was a knight supposed to protect?
24476.e: A good knight was supposed to help the weak, the poor, widows and orphans. That was part of the ideals of knighthood.
24476.m: A knight was supposed to protect the weak.

24477.q: Which word does the word “courteous” come from?
24477.e: At a prince’s court, you had to behave well. That is why “courteous” comes from the word “court”.
24477.m: The word courteous comes from the word court.

24478.q: Which virtue means being brave in danger?
24478.e: Bravery means acting courageously in danger. This virtue was very important for knights.

24479.q: Which virtue means keeping to the right measure and not overdoing things?
24479.e: Moderation means not overdoing it with food, drink or anger. In the Middle Ages this was called “mâze”.
24479.m: Moderation means keeping to the right measure.

24480.q: A good knight was supposed to be generous. What does that mean?
24480.e: A noble knight was supposed to be glad to give things to others. This virtue was called generosity.
24480.m: Being generous means being happy to share.

24481.q: What did a knight lose if he was a coward or broke his word?
24481.e: Honour was very important to a knight. Anyone who was cowardly or lied was no longer respected by the others.
24481.m: A knight did not want to lose his honour.

a: The unmarried daughter of a castle lord
24482.e: A castle maiden is the daughter of a castle lord who is not yet married. She lived with her family in the castle.
24482.m: A castle maiden is an unmarried daughter living in the castle.

24483.q: What did girls in a castle often learn?
24483.e: Girls in the castle learned needlework such as spinning, weaving and embroidery. They also learned good manners.
24483.m: Castle maidens often learned spinning and embroidery.

24484.q: What do you call the wife of a castle lord?
24484.e: The wife of the castle lord is called the lady of the castle. She had a lot of say in the castle.
24484.m: The wife of the castle lord is called the lady of the castle.

24485.q: Who often ran the castle when the lord was away at war?
24485.e: When the lord was away, his wife often ran the castle. She took care of supplies, servants and order.
24485.m: The lady of the castle often ran it when her husband was away.

24486.q: Who usually decided whom a castle maiden should marry?
24486.e: In noble families, marriages were often decided by the parents. It was about land, power and alliances.
24486.m: Usually the family decided whom a castle maiden married.

24487.q: Which board game did nobles like to play in the castle?
24487.e: Chess came to Europe in the Middle Ages and became very popular with the nobility. Noblewomen often played chess too.
24487.m: Chess was popular with nobles in the Middle Ages.

24488.q: Which hat do castle maidens often wear in pictures from the late Middle Ages?
24488.e: In the late Middle Ages, noblewomen sometimes wore a tall pointed hat. A fine veil often hung from it.
24488.m: Noblewomen sometimes wore a tall pointed hat.

24489.q: What could noblewomen in the Middle Ages often do better than many knights?
24489.e: Many noblewomen learned to read, for example from prayer books. Many knights, on the other hand, could not read.

24490.e: A herald delivered his lord’s messages. He also announced important news in public.
24490.m: A herald was a messenger and announcer.

24491.q: Who knew a lot about coats of arms in the Middle Ages?
24491.e: The herald had to know the knights’ coats of arms. That way he knew who was at the tournament or on the battlefield.
24491.m: A herald knew the knights’ coats of arms.

24492.q: What did the herald announce at a tournament?
24492.e: At the tournament, the herald introduced the knights and called out their names. He also made sure the rules were kept.
24492.m: At tournaments, the herald called out the knights’ names.

24493.q: Which word for the study of coats of arms comes from the word “herald”?
24493.e: The study of coats of arms is called heraldry. The name comes from the heralds, who knew all about coats of arms.
24493.m: Heraldry is named after the herald.

24494.q: What was the rule for a herald who brought a message to the enemy?
a: Nobody was allowed to harm him.
He had to be locked up.
24494.e: A herald was considered untouchable. Even the enemy was not allowed to harm him, so that messages arrived safely.
24494.m: Nobody was allowed to harm a herald.

24495.q: What did a herald wear over his clothes?
a: A tunic with his lord’s coat of arms
24495.e: The herald wore a tabard with his lord’s coat of arms. That way everyone could see on whose behalf he came.
24495.m: A herald wore his lord’s coat of arms.

24496.q: What was often used to announce a herald?
24496.e: Before the herald spoke, trumpeters often played. That way everyone listened.

24497.q: Where did a herald often announce the ruler’s orders?
24497.e: Many people gathered in the market square. There the herald called out orders and news.
24497.m: The herald announced news in the market square.

24498.q: What is the round table of King Arthur and his knights called?
24498.e: King Arthur sat with his knights at the Round Table. At a round table, nobody was more important than anyone else.
24498.m: At the Round Table, all knights were equally important.

24499.q: What is the name of King Arthur’s famous sword?
24499.e: Excalibur is King Arthur’s magic sword. In some stories he received it from the Lady of the Lake.
24499.m: King Arthur’s sword is called Excalibur.

24500.q: In the legend, what did the young Arthur pull a sword out of?
24500.e: Only the true king could pull the sword from the stone. The young Arthur managed it.
24500.m: Arthur pulled the sword from the stone.

24501.q: What is the name of the wizard who helps King Arthur?
24501.e: Merlin is the wise wizard in the Arthurian legends. He advised King Arthur.

24502.q: What is the name of King Arthur’s castle?
24502.e: Camelot is King Arthur’s castle and court. The Round Table stood there too.
24502.m: King Arthur’s castle is called Camelot.

24503.q: What is the name of King Arthur’s wife?
24503.e: Guinevere is the queen and Arthur’s wife. In German she is also called Ginover.

24504.q: Which knight of the Round Table fell in love with the queen?
24504.e: Lancelot was one of Arthur’s best knights. He fell in love with Queen Guinevere.

24505.q: In many stories, what were the knights of the Round Table searching for?
24505.e: The Holy Grail is a mysterious vessel. Many knights of the Round Table set out to search for it.
24505.m: Arthur’s knights searched for the Holy Grail.

24506.q: Which country do the legends of King Arthur come from?
24506.e: The Arthurian legends come from Britain. Later they were told all over Europe.
24506.m: The legends of King Arthur come from Britain.

24507.q: In which forest did Robin Hood live?
24507.e: Robin Hood lived with his friends in Sherwood Forest. This forest is near the town of Nottingham.
24507.m: Robin Hood lived in Sherwood Forest.

24508.q: In the stories, whom did Robin Hood take money from to give to the poor?
24508.e: Robin Hood took money from the rich and gave it to the poor. That is why he is a hero in many stories.
24508.m: Robin Hood took from the rich and gave to the poor.

24509.q: Which weapon was Robin Hood especially good with?
24509.e: Robin Hood was a very good archer. His arrows almost always hit the target.
24509.m: Robin Hood was a master with bow and arrow.

24510.q: Who is Robin Hood’s great enemy?
24510.e: The Sheriff of Nottingham wants to catch Robin Hood. In the stories he is his greatest enemy.
24510.m: The Sheriff of Nottingham hunts Robin Hood.

24511.q: What is the name of Robin Hood’s sweetheart?
24511.e: Maid Marian is Robin Hood’s sweetheart. In some stories she is called Lady Marian.

24513.q: Which of Robin Hood’s friends is a fat, cheerful monk?
24513.e: Friar Tuck is a monk who lives in the forest with Robin Hood. He loves eating and laughing.
24513.m: Friar Tuck is the monk with Robin Hood.

24514.q: What colour are Robin Hood’s clothes usually?
24514.e: Robin Hood usually wears green clothes. That way he is well hidden in the forest.

24515.q: In which country are the stories of Robin Hood set?
24515.e: The stories of Robin Hood are set in England. The town of Nottingham is there.
24515.m: Robin Hood is a hero from England.

a: A poet and singer of love songs
A guard at the castle gate
24516.e: A minnesinger wrote songs and performed them himself. He was both poet and singer.

24517.q: What does the old German word “Minne” mean?
24517.e: “Minne” is an old German word for love. So Minnesang means love song.
24517.m: Minne is an old word for love.

24518.q: Whom did a minnesinger usually sing his songs for?
24518.e: In his songs, the minnesinger praised a noble lady. Often she was out of his reach.
24518.m: Minnesingers sang for a noble lady.

24519.q: Who is probably the most famous minnesinger?
24519.e: This poet lived around 1200. He is considered the most famous minnesinger.
24519.m: Walther von der Vogelweide was a famous minnesinger.

24520.q: In which Swiss city was the famous song manuscript “Codex Manesse” created?
24520.e: The Codex Manesse was written in Zurich around 1300. It contains songs and colourful pictures of many minnesingers.
24520.m: The Codex Manesse was created in Zurich.

24521.q: What does the Codex Manesse contain?
24521.e: The Codex Manesse is a large manuscript of songs. It contains songs and colourful pictures of many minnesingers.
24521.m: The Codex Manesse contains songs by minnesingers.

24522.q: In which period did the minnesingers live?
a: In the time of the lake dwellers
24522.e: The minnesingers lived in the Middle Ages, especially around the year 1200. They sang at the courts of the nobility.
24522.m: Minnesingers lived in the Middle Ages.

24523.q: Where did minnesingers perform their songs?
a: At the courts of the nobility
24523.e: Minnesingers travelled from court to court. There they sang for the nobles and their guests.
24523.m: Minnesingers sang at the courts of the nobility.

24524.q: In many castles, where did the keep stand?
a: On the side where enemies attacked
In the middle of the moat
24524.e: Many keeps stood on the side from which an attack was most likely to come. That way the strong tower protected the castle like a shield.
24524.m: The keep often stood on the most exposed side of the castle.

24525.q: What could the keep be used for if enemies got into the castle?
24525.e: If the enemies were already in the castle courtyard, the people living there could flee into the keep. How often this really happened is disputed among researchers.
24525.m: The keep was the last refuge of the castle’s inhabitants.

24526.q: Where was the entrance of many keeps?
24526.e: The entrance was often several metres up in the wall. That made it hard for enemies to get in.
24526.m: Many keeps had an entrance high up in the wall.

24527.q: How did people often get up to the high entrance of the keep?
a: Through a tunnel in the ground
24527.e: People climbed up a ladder or a wooden staircase. When there was danger, they simply pulled it in.
24527.m: The ladder to the keep could be pulled in when there was danger.

24528.q: What could a guard at the top of the castle’s tallest tower do well?
24528.e: From the tall tower, the guard could see a long way. That way he spotted enemies early.
24528.m: From the tall castle tower you could see enemies from far away.

24529.q: What do you call a dark prison right at the bottom of a castle tower?
24529.e: A dungeon is a dark prison room without a door. But the room at the very bottom of the tower was often just used for storage.
24529.m: A dungeon is a dark prison in the castle.

24530.q: What do you call a watchman who kept a lookout at the top of a tower?
24530.e: The tower watchman kept watch at the top of the tower. If he saw enemies or fire, he raised the alarm.
24530.m: The tower watchman kept watch at the top of the tower.

24531.q: Why did a keep have very thick walls?
a: So that it could withstand attacks
So that it stayed warm inside
So that it could be built taller
So that supplies could be stored in the walls
24531.e: Thick walls held out against stones and battering rams for a long time. Some walls were several metres thick.
24531.m: Thick walls protected the keep from attacks.

24532.q: What did attackers often try to do with the moat?
a: Fill it with earth and wood
24532.e: A filled-in moat was no longer an obstacle. Then the attackers could get right up to the wall.
24532.m: Attackers filled in the moat to reach the wall.

24533.q: What is the ditch called that separates a castle on a ridge from the rest of the mountain?
24533.e: The neck ditch separated the castle from the rest of the mountain. That way enemies could not simply walk along the ridge to the castle.
24533.m: The neck ditch separates the castle from the mountain.

24534.q: Why was a ditch built around the castle?
a: It made it hard for enemies to reach the wall
There needed to be room for fish
The children could swim in it
Ships were meant to moor there
24534.e: The ditch was an obstacle. Attackers with ladders and battering rams could not get straight to the wall.
24534.m: The ditch keeps attackers away from the castle wall.

24535.q: What do you call a castle moat without water?
24535.e: Many castles on mountains had a ditch without water. It is called a dry moat.
24535.m: A moat without water is called a dry moat.

24536.q: Which part of the castle did the drawbridge lead to?
24536.e: The drawbridge led across the moat straight to the gate. When it was pulled up, it closed the entrance.
24536.m: The drawbridge leads across the moat to the castle gate.

24537.q: What was used to pull up the drawbridge?
24537.e: The bridge hung on chains or ropes. It was pulled up with a winch.
24537.m: The drawbridge was pulled up with chains or ropes.

24538.q: What helped to pull up the heavy drawbridge more easily?
24538.e: Some drawbridges had heavy counterweights. They pulled the bridge up almost by themselves.
24538.m: Counterweights make pulling it up easier.

24539.q: What was a drawbridge usually made of?
24539.e: Wood was light enough for the bridge to be pulled up. It was often strengthened with iron.
24539.m: The drawbridge was usually made of wood.

24540.q: What could be quickly lowered from above in the castle gateway to block it?
24540.e: The portcullis came crashing down in the gateway. That way the entrance was quickly blocked.
24540.m: The portcullis quickly blocks the castle gate.

24541.e: The portcullis blocked the passage through the gate. It protected the way into the castle.
24541.m: The portcullis is in the castle gateway.

24542.q: What was a portcullis made of?
24542.e: Portcullises were made of oak with iron fittings, or entirely of iron. They were very heavy.
24542.m: A portcullis was made of wood and iron.

24543.q: Which animals often pulled the carts with heavy stones to the building site?
24543.e: Oxen are very strong and have great stamina. In the Middle Ages they pulled heavy wagons with stones and wood.
24543.m: Oxen pulled heavy loads to the building site.

24544.q: What did the portcullis often have at the bottom?
24544.e: The bars ended in spikes at the bottom. That way the grille dug into the ground.
24544.m: The portcullis had pointed ends at the bottom.

24545.q: Why did the portcullis close so quickly?
a: It fell down under its own weight
Servants pushed it shut from the side
A water wheel turned it shut
Oxen pulled it shut with ropes
24545.e: You only had to let go of the grille. Because of its great weight, it fell down by itself.
24545.m: The heavy portcullis falls under its own weight.

24546.q: Where was the portcullis when the gate was open?
a: In the room above the gate
24546.e: The grille was pulled up into a room above the gate. From there it could be lowered quickly.
24546.m: The raised portcullis waited above the gate.

24547.q: Some castles had two portcullises in the gateway. What could they do with them?
24547.e: If the guards lowered both grilles, the attackers were trapped in between. They could go neither forwards nor back.
24547.m: Two portcullises could trap enemies in the gateway.

24548.q: What are the gaps between the raised parts of the battlements called?
24548.e: The gaps between the raised parts (merlons) are called crenels or embrasures. The defenders shot through them.
24548.m: The gaps in the battlements are called crenels.

24549.e: A defender could hide behind the raised part of the battlements. He could shoot through the gap next to it.
24549.m: Battlements protected the defenders on the wall.

24550.q: What is a narrow slit in the wall that you could shoot through called?
24550.e: An arrow slit is wide on the inside and narrow on the outside. That way you could shoot out and still be protected.
24550.m: Through an arrow slit you could shoot while staying protected.

24551.q: Which weapon did defenders often shoot from the battlements?
24551.e: Archers stood behind the battlements. Later there were also crossbows.
24551.m: From the battlements, people shot with bows and arrows.

24552.q: What is the walkway along the top of the castle wall called?
24552.e: On the wall walk, the defenders could move along the wall. It was behind the battlements.
24552.m: The wall walk is the walkway on top of the wall.

24553.q: Who walked up and down on the wall walk?
24553.e: Guards kept a lookout on the wall walk. During an attack, soldiers defended the castle from there.
24553.m: Guards kept a lookout on the wall walk.

24554.q: What did some wall walks have to protect against rain and arrows?
24554.e: Many wall walks were covered with a wooden roof. That protected against the weather and arrows from above.
24554.m: A roof protected some wall walks.

26197.q: What kind of people were the Alemanni?
26197.e: The Alemanni were a Germanic people. They first lived in what is now southern Germany.
26197.m: The Alemanni were a Germanic people.

26198.q: In which part of Switzerland did the Alemanni settle?
26198.e: The Alemanni settled mainly in the north and east of today’s Switzerland. This area is now part of German-speaking Switzerland.
26198.m: The Alemanni lived in German-speaking Switzerland.

26199.q: Which language comes from the language of the Alemanni?
26199.e: The Alemanni spoke a Germanic language. Our Swiss German dialects developed from it.
26199.m: Swiss German comes from the Alemanni.

26200.q: Who ruled Switzerland before the Alemanni came?
26200.e: Before the Alemanni, the area belonged to the Roman Empire. When the Romans left, the Alemanni came.
26200.m: After the Romans came the Alemanni.

26201.q: Across which river did the Alemanni come into Switzerland?
26201.e: The Alemanni first lived north of the Rhine. Later they crossed the Rhine and moved south.
26201.m: The Alemanni came across the Rhine.

26202.q: How did most Alemanni make their living?
26202.e: Most Alemanni were farmers. They kept animals and grew grain.

26203.q: Which ending of Swiss place names often recalls the Alemanni?
26203.e: Many villages ending in “-ingen” were founded by Alemanni. One example is Ermatingen in Thurgau.
26203.m: Place names ending in “-ingen” often recall the Alemanni.

26204.q: Where did the Alemanni usually build their houses?
26204.e: The Alemanni did not like big towns. They preferred to live in small villages and farmsteads.
26204.m: The Alemanni lived in small villages.

26205.q: In which part of Switzerland did the Burgundians live?
26205.e: The Romans gave the Burgundians land in the west of today’s Switzerland. There they founded their kingdom.
26205.m: The Burgundians lived in western Switzerland.

26206.q: On which lake did the Burgundians settle?
26206.e: The Burgundians settled around Lake Geneva. Later their kingdom became much larger.
26206.m: The Burgundians lived on Lake Geneva.

26207.q: Which language did the Burgundians take over from the Romans?
26207.e: The Burgundians learned the Latin of the people who already lived there. Their own Germanic language was lost.
26207.m: The Burgundians took over the language of the Romans.

26208.q: Which language is spoken today where the Burgundians lived?
26208.e: French developed from the Latin spoken in western Switzerland. That is why French is spoken there today.
26208.m: French is spoken in western Switzerland.

26209.q: What kind of people were the Burgundians originally?
26209.e: The Burgundians came from the north as a Germanic people. They then lived together with the Romans.
26209.m: The Burgundians were also a Germanic people.

26210.q: Which monastery did the Burgundian king Sigismund found in Valais?
26210.e: King Sigismund founded the Abbey of Saint-Maurice in the year 515. Members of a religious order still live and pray there today.
26210.m: The Abbey of Saint-Maurice in Valais is very old.

26211.q: What was the faith of the Burgundians in their kingdom?
26211.e: The Burgundians were Christians. They built churches and monasteries.

26212.q: Which town played an important role for the Burgundians?
26212.e: Geneva was an important Burgundian town. The kings lived there at times.
26212.m: Geneva is an old Burgundian town.

26213.e: Gallus lived as a hermit monk in the forest and prayed a lot.

26214.q: According to old tradition, which country did the monk Gallus come from?
26214.e: Old stories say that Gallus came from Ireland. Some researchers today think he might also have come from Alsace.

26215.q: According to legend, which animal helped Gallus?
26215.e: According to legend, a bear fetched wood for Gallus’s fire. Afterwards the bear had to leave the place.
26215.m: A bear helped the monk Gallus.

26216.q: What did Gallus give the bear to say thank you?
26216.e: Gallus gave the bear a loaf of bread. In return the bear was never to show itself there again.
26216.m: The bear got bread from Gallus.

26217.q: Which town is named after Gallus?
26217.e: The town of St Gallen bears the monk’s name. It grew up around his monastery.
26217.m: St Gallen is named after Gallus.

26218.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of St Gallen?
26218.e: There is a bear on the coat of arms of the town of St Gallen. It recalls the legend of Gallus.
26218.m: The bear on the coat of arms recalls Gallus.

26219.q: By which stream did Gallus settle?
26219.e: Gallus built his cell by the Steinach stream. The town of St Gallen stands there today.

26220.q: On which day is St Gallus’ Day?
26220.e: St Gallus’ Day is on 16 October. On this day people remember the monk Gallus.
26220.m: St Gallus’ Day is in October.

26221.q: What can you see in the Abbey Library of St Gallen?
26221.e: The Abbey Library is a very old library. Many of its books were written by hand more than 1,000 years ago.
26221.m: The Abbey Library has old books.

26222.q: What do visitors put over their shoes in the great hall of the Abbey Library of St Gallen?
26222.e: Visitors wear big felt slippers. This protects the beautiful wooden floor.
26222.m: In the Abbey Library you wear felt slippers.

26223.q: Who used to write the books in the monastery of St Gallen?
26223.e: Monks copied the books with quill and ink. This often took many months.
26223.m: Monks wrote the books by hand.

26224.q: What did monks write their books on in the Middle Ages?
26224.e: Parchment is a thin animal skin. The monks wrote their books on it.
26224.m: Parchment is made from animal skin.

26225.q: Which mummy lies in the Abbey Library of St Gallen?
a: An ice mummy from the Alps
26225.e: The Egyptian mummy Shepenese lies in the Abbey Library. She is over 2,500 years old.
26225.m: There is an Egyptian mummy in St Gallen.

26226.q: What is the magnificent hall of the Abbey Library called?
26226.e: The great library hall is built in the Baroque style. It has a lot of wood and colourful ceiling paintings.
26226.m: The Baroque Hall is very magnificent.

26227.q: What distinction has the Abbey District of St Gallen had since 1983?
26227.e: The Abbey District with its church and library has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983. It is important for the whole world.
26227.m: The Abbey District of St Gallen is a World Heritage Site.

26228.q: What does the Greek inscription above the door of the Abbey Library roughly mean?
26228.e: Above the door it says in Greek “healing place of the soul”. People often say “pharmacy of the soul”.
26228.m: Books are like medicine for the soul.

26229.q: What does the Plan of St Gall show?
26229.e: The plan shows what an ideal monastery should look like. You can see the church, stables, gardens and workshops.
26229.m: The Plan of St Gall shows a whole monastery.

26230.q: What was the Plan of St Gall drawn on?
26230.e: The plan was drawn about 1,200 years ago on parchment, that is, thin animal skin. It is made of several pieces sewn together.
26230.m: The Plan of St Gall is drawn on parchment.

26231.q: Roughly how old is the Plan of St Gall?
26231.e: The plan was made around the year 825. So it is around 1,200 years old.
26231.m: The Plan of St Gall is around 1,200 years old.

26232.q: On which island did someone draw the Plan of St Gall?
26232.e: The plan came from the monastery of Reichenau on Lake Constance. Then it went to St Gallen.
26232.m: The Plan of St Gall comes from Reichenau.

26233.q: Did they build the monastery of St Gallen exactly according to the plan at that time?
a: No, the plan served as a model
26233.e: The plan served as a model and an idea. The church built in St Gallen around 830 looked different.
26233.m: The Plan of St Gall was an ideal plan.

26234.q: What is special about the Plan of St Gall?
a: It is the oldest drawn plan of a monastery
It is the oldest map of Switzerland
It is the first printed town map
It shows the largest monastery in Europe
26234.e: There is no older drawing of a monastery from the Middle Ages. That is why the plan is so valuable.
26234.m: The Plan of St Gall is an ancient drawing of a monastery.

26235.q: Where is the Plan of St Gall kept today?
a: In the Abbey Library of St Gallen
In the Federal Palace in Bern
In the National Museum in Zurich
26235.e: The plan is kept in the Abbey Library of St Gallen. It is well protected there.
26235.m: The Plan of St Gall is kept in St Gallen.

26236.q: In which country is a monastery being built today at Campus Galli according to the Plan of St Gall?
26236.e: At Campus Galli in Messkirch, people are building a monastery following the plan. They work with old tools.
26236.m: At Campus Galli the Plan of St Gall is being rebuilt.

26237.q: In which canton is the monastery of Einsiedeln?
26237.e: Einsiedeln is in the canton of Schwyz. The monastery is very large and well known.
26237.m: The monastery of Einsiedeln is in the canton of Schwyz.

26238.q: Which hermit lived in this place before the monastery?
26238.e: The monk Meinrad lived there alone in the forest. Later the monastery was built where he had lived.
26238.m: Meinrad lived as a hermit in the Dark Forest.

26240.q: Which famous figure stands in the church of Einsiedeln?
26240.e: The Black Madonna stands in a small chapel in the monastery church. Many people come to see her and to pray.
26240.m: The Black Madonna is in Einsiedeln.

26241.q: Who lives in the monastery of Einsiedeln?
26241.e: Monks live in the monastery of Einsiedeln. They are Benedictines and pray and work there.

26242.q: Why have people travelled to Einsiedeln for many hundreds of years?
a: To buy salt at the market
26242.e: Einsiedeln is a place of pilgrimage. Pilgrims have been coming there to pray for many centuries.
26242.m: Einsiedeln is a place of pilgrimage.

26243.q: In which century was the monastery of Einsiedeln founded?
26243.e: The monastery was founded in the year 934. That is in the 10th century.
26243.m: The monastery of Einsiedeln is over 1,000 years old.

26244.q: Which animals have the monks of Einsiedeln bred for a long time?
26244.e: The monastery of Einsiedeln has one of the oldest horse studs in Europe. The horses are called Einsiedlers.
26244.m: Einsiedeln is also known for its horses.

26245.q: In which canton is the monastery of Müstair?
26245.e: Müstair is in the canton of the Grisons. The village is very close to the border with Italy.
26245.m: The monastery of Müstair is in the Grisons.

26246.q: Which famous king is said to have founded the monastery of Müstair?
26246.e: Legend says that Charlemagne founded the monastery. There is a statue of him in the church.
26246.m: Charlemagne is said to have founded Müstair.

26247.q: What is the monastery church of Müstair famous for?
a: An organ with a thousand pipes
26247.e: The church has wall paintings from the time of Charlemagne. They are over 1,200 years old.

26248.q: Who lives in the monastery of Müstair today?
26248.e: Today Benedictine sisters live in the monastery. They are nuns.
26248.m: Nuns live in the monastery of Müstair.

26249.q: Since which year has the monastery of Müstair been a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
26249.e: The monastery of Müstair became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983. It is important for the whole world.
26249.m: Müstair has been a World Heritage Site since 1983.

26250.q: The monastery of Müstair is close to which country?
26250.e: Müstair is in the far east of Switzerland. Italy begins just a few steps away.
26250.m: Müstair is on the border with Italy.

26251.e: Müstair comes from the Latin word for monastery. The village is named after the monastery.

26252.q: Roughly how old is the monastery of Müstair?
26252.e: The monastery was founded around the year 775. So it is around 1,250 years old.
26252.m: The monastery of Müstair is very old.

26253.q: Which kingdom did Queen Bertha rule with her husband?
26253.e: Bertha was Queen of Burgundy. Today’s western Switzerland also belonged to this kingdom.
26253.m: Bertha ruled as Queen of Burgundy.

26254.q: According to legend, what did Queen Bertha do on her horse?
26254.e: The legend says that Bertha rode through the land spinning wool as she went. She was hard-working and kind to people.
26254.m: Queen Bertha spun wool on horseback.

26255.q: In which town is Queen Bertha buried?
26255.e: Bertha was buried in Payerne. A large old abbey church stands there.

26256.q: In which period did Queen Bertha live?
26256.e: Bertha lived more than 1,000 years ago, in the early Middle Ages. At that time there were kings, castles and monasteries.
26256.m: Queen Bertha lived in the Middle Ages.

26257.q: Which canton is Queen Bertha a symbol of?
26257.e: In the 19th century Bertha became a symbol of the canton of Vaud. Payerne is in Vaud.
26257.m: Queen Bertha is a symbol of Vaud.

26258.q: What did Bertha’s daughter Adelaide later become?
26258.e: Bertha’s daughter Adelaide married Emperor Otto I. This made her an empress.
26258.m: Bertha’s daughter Adelaide became an empress.

26259.q: How is Queen Bertha mainly described in the legend?
a: As a good and hard-working queen
26259.e: In the stories Bertha is a good queen. She helped the poor.
26259.m: Bertha is known as a good queen.

26260.q: Roughly when did Queen Bertha live?
26260.e: Bertha lived in the 10th century. She died after the year 966.
26260.m: Bertha lived more than 1,000 years ago.

26261.e: The Zähringens were a powerful family of dukes. They ruled large areas in southern Germany and Switzerland.

26262.q: What are the Zähringens known for in Switzerland?
26262.e: The Zähringens founded several towns in the Swiss Plateau. This helped them to protect and rule their land better.

26263.q: Which town in the Üechtland did the Zähringens found in 1157?
26263.e: Duke Berthold IV founded the town of Fribourg in the Üechtland in 1157. It has the same name as Freiburg im Breisgau.

26264.q: Which town on the river Emme belonged to the Zähringens?
26264.e: Burgdorf lies on the Emme. The Zähringens built a castle there and made the place a town.

26265.q: Which town on Lake Thun did the Zähringens expand?
26265.e: The Zähringens built the castle in Thun and enlarged the town. Thun lies where the Aare flows out of Lake Thun.

26266.q: Which town on Lake Murten did the Zähringens found?
26266.e: Murten was newly founded by Duke Berthold IV of Zähringen. The town still has a long town wall today.

26268.q: What does the Zähringen Fountain in Bern show?
26268.e: On top of the Zähringen Fountain stands a bear in a knight’s armour. It recalls the founder of Bern.
26268.m: The Zähringen Fountain shows a bear.

26269.q: Who founded the city of Bern?
26269.e: Duke Berthold V of Zähringen founded Bern. He was the last duke of his family.

26270.q: In which year was Bern founded?
26270.e: Bern dates from 1191. A hundred years later the Swiss Confederation was formed.

26271.q: According to legend, which animal gave Bern its name?
26271.e: The founder wanted to name the town after the first animal killed in the hunt. The first animal was a bear.
26271.m: Bern is named after the bear.

26272.q: Where can visitors see live bears in Bern today?
26272.e: Bears live in the Bear Park by the Aare. They used to live in the cramped bear pit.
26272.m: Bears live in Bern’s Bear Park.

26273.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of the canton of Bern?
26273.e: On the Bern coat of arms a black bear walks along a yellow stripe. It recalls the legend.
26273.m: The bear is Bern’s heraldic animal.

26274.q: Since when has Bern’s Old Town been a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
26274.e: Bern’s Old Town was added to the World Heritage list in 1983. It has many old streets with arcades.
26274.m: Bern’s Old Town is a World Heritage Site.

26275.q: On which lake is Chillon Castle?
26275.e: Chillon Castle stands on the shore of Lake Geneva. It is near Montreux.
26275.m: Chillon Castle is on Lake Geneva.

26276.q: What was Chillon Castle built on?
a: On a rock in the lake
26276.e: The castle stands on a small rocky island in the water. This kept it well protected.
26276.m: Chillon stands on a rock in the lake.

26277.q: Which family turned Chillon Castle into a large fortress?
26277.e: The Counts of Savoy enlarged Chillon in the Middle Ages. From there they controlled the road along the lake.
26277.m: The House of Savoy enlarged Chillon.

26278.q: In which canton is Chillon Castle?
26278.e: Chillon belongs to the municipality of Veytaux in the canton of Vaud. That is in western Switzerland.

26279.q: Which prisoner sat in the dungeon of Chillon Castle?
26279.e: François Bonivard spent several years chained up in Chillon. He had opposed the Duke of Savoy.
26279.m: Bonivard was a prisoner in Chillon.

26281.q: According to legend, what did Lord Byron carve into a pillar at Chillon?
26281.e: In the dungeon the name “Byron” is carved into a pillar. People say he carved it himself.
26281.m: Byron’s name is on a pillar.

26282.e: In 1536 the Bernese conquered Vaud and Chillon too. After that the castle belonged to Bern for a long time.

26283.q: In which gorge is the Devil’s Bridge?
26283.e: The Devil’s Bridge crosses the Schöllenen Gorge. The gorge is very narrow and steep.
26283.m: The Devil’s Bridge is in the Schöllenen.

26284.q: In which canton is the Devil’s Bridge?
26284.e: The Schöllenen Gorge is in the canton of Uri. It leads to Andermatt.
26284.m: The Devil’s Bridge is in the canton of Uri.

26285.q: Which river does the Devil’s Bridge cross?
26285.e: The Reuss rushes beneath the Devil’s Bridge. It flows north through the gorge.
26285.m: The Devil’s Bridge crosses the Reuss.

26286.q: According to legend, who built the bridge?
26286.e: The people of Uri could not manage to build it. According to legend, the Devil built the bridge for them.
26286.m: According to legend, the Devil built the bridge.

26287.q: What did the Devil want as payment for the bridge?
26287.e: The Devil wanted the soul of whoever crossed the bridge first. That would be his reward.
26287.m: The Devil wanted the first soul.

26288.q: Which animal did the people of Uri send across the Devil’s Bridge first?
26288.e: The clever people of Uri let a billy goat run across the bridge first. So the Devil did not get a human.
26288.m: A billy goat outwitted the Devil.

26289.q: In the legend, what did the angry Devil want to do with a huge stone?
26289.e: The furious Devil wanted to destroy the bridge with a rock. But he missed it. The Devil’s Stone lies near Göschenen today.
26289.m: The Devil wanted to destroy the bridge with a stone.

26290.q: Which pass does the route over the Devil’s Bridge lead to?
26290.e: The Devil’s Bridge lies on the route over the Gotthard Pass. This route connects the north with the south.
26290.m: The Devil’s Bridge is on the Gotthard route.

26291.q: With which other monk did Gallus travel through Europe?
26291.e: Gallus was a companion of the Irish monk Columbanus. Later they went their separate ways.

26292.q: Who founded the monastery of St Gallen in 719 at the place where Gallus had lived?
26292.e: About 100 years after Gallus, Otmar founded a monastery there. He became the first abbot.
26292.m: Otmar founded the monastery of St Gallen.

26293.e: Today you can visit Chillon Castle. It is a museum and one of the best-known castles in Switzerland.
26293.m: Chillon Castle is a museum today.

26294.q: Which Russian general fought at the Devil’s Bridge in 1799?
26294.e: The Russian general Suvorov fought against the French in the Schöllenen in 1799. A monument carved into the rock recalls this.
26294.m: There is a monument to Suvorov in the Schöllenen.

26295.q: According to legend, who did Winkelried ask the others to look after after his death?
26295.e: According to legend, Winkelried called out that they should look after his wife and children.
26295.m: Winkelried thought of his wife and children.

26296.q: Which building stands on the battlefield at Sempach today?
26296.e: The Battle Chapel stands on the battlefield. The battle is remembered there every year.
26296.m: A chapel stands on the battlefield at Sempach.

26297.q: What is Winkelried said to have grabbed with his arms?
26297.e: He is said to have grabbed several of the knights’ lances and pressed them to his chest. This allowed the Confederates to attack.
26297.m: Winkelried is said to have grabbed the enemy’s lances.

26298.q: What did Winkelried want to open for his friends?
26298.e: He is said to have shouted that he would make a path for the Confederates. They could attack through this gap.
26298.m: Winkelried wanted to open a path for the Confederates.

26299.q: Which area is Arnold Winkelried said to have come from?
26299.e: According to tradition, Winkelried was a man from Unterwalden, more precisely from Nidwalden.

26300.q: What reminds people of Arnold Winkelried in Stans?
26300.e: A Winkelried monument has stood on the village square in Stans since 1865.

26301.q: Who did the Confederates fight at Sempach?
26301.e: At Sempach the Confederates fought the Habsburg army of knights.
26301.m: At Sempach the Confederates defeated the Habsburgs.

26302.q: What do you call an old hero story like Winkelried’s, which may not have happened exactly like that?
26302.e: Nobody knows for sure whether Winkelried really lived. His story is told as a legend.
26302.m: The story of Winkelried is a legend.

26303.q: According to legend, what happened to Winkelried himself?
26303.e: Winkelried suffered fatal wounds. But his sacrifice helped the others to victory.
26303.m: According to legend, Winkelried died in the battle.

26304.q: What do many people call Niklaus von Flüe?
26304.e: Niklaus von Flüe lived as a hermit and is therefore called Brother Klaus.
26304.m: Niklaus von Flüe is also called Brother Klaus.

26305.q: In which canton did Brother Klaus live?
26305.e: Brother Klaus came into the world in 1417 near Sachseln. That is in today’s canton of Obwalden.

26306.q: In which gorge did Brother Klaus live as a hermit?
26306.e: Brother Klaus lived in a small cell in the Ranft, a gorge near Sachseln.
26306.m: Brother Klaus lived in the Ranft.

a: Someone who lives alone and prays
26307.e: A hermit withdraws from other people to live quietly and pray.
26307.m: A hermit lives alone and prays a lot.

26308.q: How many children did Brother Klaus have?
26308.e: Before he became a hermit, he was a farmer and had ten children with his wife.

26309.q: What name did Brother Klaus’s wife have?
26309.e: His wife was Dorothee Wyss. She agreed to him becoming a hermit.
26309.m: Brother Klaus’s wife had the name Dorothee.

26310.q: What is Brother Klaus said not to have done for many years?
26310.e: It is said that he ate nothing for around 19 years.
26310.m: Brother Klaus is said to have eaten nothing for many years.

26311.q: What happened to Brother Klaus in 1947?
a: He got a monument in Rome
26311.e: Pope Pius XII declared Brother Klaus a saint in 1947.
26311.m: Brother Klaus has been a saint since 1947.

26312.q: Who is Brother Klaus for many people in Switzerland?
a: The patron saint of the country
26312.e: The Catholic Church honours Brother Klaus as the patron saint of Switzerland.
26312.m: Brother Klaus is the patron saint of Switzerland.

26313.q: In which year was the Covenant of Stans agreed?
26313.e: The Covenant of Stans was agreed in December 1481.
26313.m: The Covenant of Stans dates from 1481.

26314.e: A covenant is an agreement. In it the members agreed on rules with each other.

26315.q: Who was quarrelling before the Covenant of Stans?
a: The town cantons and the rural cantons
26315.e: Towns such as Zurich and Bern quarrelled with rural cantons such as Uri and Schwyz.
26315.m: In Stans the towns and rural cantons came to an agreement.

26316.q: What, among other things, did the members argue about before 1481?
26316.e: After the wars against Burgundy, it was unclear how the captured treasures should be shared.
26316.m: The members argued about the war booty.

26317.q: Which two towns were admitted to the Confederation in 1481?
26317.e: With the Covenant of Stans, Fribourg and Solothurn became new members of the Confederation.

26318.q: Who is said to have helped the Confederates reach agreement in Stans in 1481 with good advice?
26318.e: A priest brought the delegates a message from Niklaus von Flüe. After that they reached an agreement.
26318.m: A hermit’s advice helped the agreement in Stans.

26319.q: What was the assembly of delegates from the members that met in Stans in 1481 called?
26319.e: At the Diet, representatives of all the members met to discuss common questions.
26319.m: The Diet was the assembly of the old Confederates.

26320.q: What threatened before the agreement in Stans?
26320.e: The quarrel was so bad that a war between their own members seemed possible. The covenant prevented it.
26320.m: The Covenant of Stans prevented an armed conflict.

26321.q: In which city is the Chapel Bridge?
26321.e: The Chapel Bridge is the best-known landmark of the city of Lucerne.
26321.m: The Chapel Bridge is in Lucerne.

26322.q: Which river does the Chapel Bridge cross?
26322.e: The bridge crosses the Reuss where it flows out of Lake Lucerne.
26322.m: The Chapel Bridge crosses the Reuss.

26323.q: What material is the Chapel Bridge made of?
26323.e: The Chapel Bridge is a covered wooden bridge. It has a tiled roof.
26323.m: The Chapel Bridge is a wooden bridge.

26324.q: What is the eight-sided tower next to the Chapel Bridge called?
26324.e: The Water Tower stands in the river next to the bridge. In the past it served, among other things, as a prison and treasury.
26324.m: The Water Tower stands next to the Chapel Bridge.

26325.q: What hangs under the roof of the Chapel Bridge?
26325.e: Triangular paintings from the 17th century hang in the roof gables. They show stories from Lucerne and Switzerland.
26325.m: Old painted pictures hang in the Chapel Bridge.

26326.q: What happened to the Chapel Bridge in 1993?
26326.e: In August 1993 a large part of the bridge burned down. It was rebuilt afterwards.

26327.q: What happened to the Chapel Bridge in the year 1993?
a: A fire destroyed a large part of it
26327.e: In 1993 a large part of the Chapel Bridge burned down. It was rebuilt just as it had been before.

26328.q: Roughly how old is the Chapel Bridge?
26328.e: The bridge was built around 1365. It is one of the oldest covered wooden bridges in Europe.
26328.m: The Chapel Bridge is over 650 years old.

26329.q: How do people vote at the Landsgemeinde?
26329.e: Anyone who agrees raises their hand. This is called a show of hands.
26329.m: At the Landsgemeinde people vote by hand.

26331.q: In which month does the Glarus Landsgemeinde normally take place?
26331.e: The Glarus Landsgemeinde usually takes place on the first Sunday in May.
26331.m: The Glarus Landsgemeinde is in May.

26332.q: What may men in Appenzell Innerrhoden bring to the Landsgemeinde as proof that they can vote?
26332.e: Traditionally, men show with a sword or sabre that they are allowed to vote. Today the voting card is also accepted.
26332.m: In Appenzell the sword counts as an old voting card.

26333.q: What is the place called where people gather in a circle at the Landsgemeinde?
26333.e: The voters stand in a large circle, known as the Ring.
26333.m: At the Landsgemeinde people stand in the Ring.

26334.e: The Landammann is the highest representative of the cantonal government and leads the Landsgemeinde.

26335.q: On which day of the week does the Landsgemeinde take place?
26335.e: In both Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden the Landsgemeinde is held on a Sunday.
26335.m: The Landsgemeinde is on a Sunday.

26336.q: What can you see on the coat of arms of the canton of Basel-Stadt?
26336.e: The Basel coat of arms shows a black Basel crook. It is a form of bishop’s staff.
26336.m: The Basel coat of arms has a bishop’s crook.

26337.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of the canton of Schaffhausen?
26337.e: The Schaffhausen coat of arms shows a black ram on a yellow background.
26337.m: A ram leaps on the Schaffhausen coat of arms.

26338.q: What does the coat of arms of the canton of Geneva show?
26338.e: The Geneva coat of arms shows half an eagle on the left and a golden key on the right.
26338.m: The Geneva coat of arms has an eagle and a key.

26339.q: Which canton has an ibex on its coat of arms?
26339.e: The coat of arms of the Grisons has three fields. One of them shows a black ibex.
26339.m: An ibex can be seen on the coat of arms of the Grisons.

26340.q: How many stars are on the coat of arms of Valais?
26340.e: The 13 stars on the Valais coat of arms stand for the districts of the canton, which used to be called Zenden.
26340.m: The Valais coat of arms has 13 stars.

26341.q: What colours does the coat of arms of the canton of Ticino have?
26341.e: The Ticino coat of arms is divided vertically: red on the left, blue on the right.
26341.m: The Ticino coat of arms is red and blue.

26342.q: Which animals are on the coat of arms of the canton of Thurgau?
26342.e: The Thurgau coat of arms shows two yellow lions on a green and white background.
26342.m: The Thurgau coat of arms has two lions.

26343.q: What colours does the coat of arms of the canton of Zurich have?
26343.e: The Zurich coat of arms is divided diagonally, white at the top and blue at the bottom.
26343.m: The Zurich coat of arms is blue and white.

26344.q: Who can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Glarus?
26344.e: The Glarus coat of arms shows Saint Fridolin as a traveller with a staff. He is the patron saint of Glarus.
26344.m: Saint Fridolin walks on the Glarus coat of arms.

26345.q: What colour is the Uri bull on the coat of arms of Uri?
26345.e: The Uri bull on the coat of arms is black. The background is yellow.

26346.q: What does the Uri bull have in its nose?
26346.e: The Uri bull on the coat of arms of Uri has a red nose ring.
26346.m: The Uri bull has a ring in its nose.

26347.q: How much of the bull can you see on the coat of arms of Uri?
26347.e: Only the bull’s head is shown on the coat of arms, so people also call it the bull’s head.
26347.m: The coat of arms of Uri shows a bull’s head.

26348.q: What colour is the Uri bull’s tongue?
26348.e: The Uri bull sticks out a red tongue.
26348.m: The Uri bull has a red tongue.

26349.q: What did the people of Uri call their great war horn?
26349.e: Uri’s war horn bore the name of Uri’s heraldic animal. It was called the “Bull of Uri”.
26349.m: Uri’s war horn had the name “Bull of Uri”.

26350.q: What did the people of Uri use their great war horn for in battle?
26350.e: A war horn is a large horn you blow. Its loud sound gave signals in battle.
26350.m: The people of Uri blew signals with the war horn.

26351.q: According to an old explanation, the name Uri comes from the “Ur”. What is an Ur?
26351.e: The Ur or aurochs was a wild ox that used to live in Europe. It is not certain whether the name Uri really comes from it.
26351.m: The Ur was a wild ox.

26352.q: How many horns does the Uri bull have on the coat of arms?
26352.e: The Uri bull on the coat of arms of Uri has two horns, like a real bull.
26352.m: The Uri bull has two horns.

26353.q: According to a well-known explanation, what does the name Habsburg mean?
26353.e: It is said that the name comes from “Habichtsburg”, meaning castle of the hawk. But this is not certain.

a: On an island in a lake
26354.e: The castle stands on the Wülpelsberg, a wooded hill.
26354.m: Habsburg Castle stands on a hill.

26355.q: Which town is near Habsburg Castle?
26355.e: Habsburg Castle is only a few kilometres from Brugg.

26356.q: What can visitors find in Habsburg Castle today?
26356.e: Today Habsburg Castle has a restaurant and a small exhibition about the castle.
26356.m: Today you can go out for a meal at Habsburg Castle.

26357.q: What did the Habsburgs later become?
26357.e: The family became very powerful. Many Habsburgs became kings and emperors in Europe.
26357.m: The Habsburgs became a powerful family of emperors.

26358.q: Which animal did the old Habsburg coat of arms show?
26358.e: The coat of arms of the Counts of Habsburg showed a red lion on a yellow background.
26358.m: The Habsburgs had a red lion on their coat of arms.

a: The castle a family is named after
A castle made of tree trunks
26359.e: Habsburg Castle is the ancestral castle of the Habsburgs. The family comes from there and is named after it.
26359.m: Habsburg Castle is the ancestral castle of the Habsburgs.

26360.q: Which monastery near Windisch did the Habsburg family found?
26360.e: Königsfelden monastery was built from 1309 on the spot where a Habsburg king had been killed.
26360.m: Königsfelden monastery was founded by the Habsburgs.

26361.q: Which nickname did Duke Charles of Burgundy have?
26361.e: People called Duke Charles of Burgundy “the Bold” because he was brave and liked to attack.
26361.m: Charles of Burgundy is known as Charles the Bold.

26362.q: Near which lakeside town did the Confederates defeat Charles in June 1476?
26362.e: In the Battle of Murten on 22 June 1476, the Confederates and their allies won.
26362.m: At Murten the Confederates defeated Charles.

26363.q: Near which town did Charles the Bold lose his treasure in March 1476?
26363.e: At Grandson the Burgundians fled and left their whole camp behind. A well-known Swiss saying goes: “At Grandson his treasure, at Murten his courage, at Nancy his blood.”
26363.m: At Grandson Charles lost his treasure.

26364.e: Grandson lies on the south-western shore of Lake Neuchâtel in the canton of Vaud.

26365.q: What does the Murten run commemorate?
a: A messenger with news of victory
26365.e: According to legend, after the Battle of Murten a messenger ran all the way to Fribourg to report the victory.
26365.m: The Murten run recalls a messenger of victory.

a: The captured treasures of Charles the Bold
The ransom for Charles the Bold
26366.e: After their victories, the Confederates took many treasures from the camp of Charles the Bold.
26366.m: The Burgundian booty is the treasure of Charles the Bold.

26367.q: What was part of the Burgundian booty?
26367.e: The booty included magnificent tapestries, tents, jewellery and tableware, among other things.
26367.m: The Burgundian booty includes magnificent tapestries.

26368.q: In which city does a history museum show famous tapestries from the Burgundian booty?
26368.e: The Bern History Museum owns precious tapestries from the Burgundian booty.
26368.m: Parts of the Burgundian booty can be seen in Bern.

26369.q: Which weapons did the Confederates capture in large numbers at Grandson?
26369.e: Charles left many cannons behind when he fled. Today they are called Burgundian cannons.
26369.m: At Grandson the Confederates captured many cannons.

26370.q: Who does the Swiss Guard protect?
26370.e: The Swiss Guard protects the Pope in the Vatican. The guards are young men from Switzerland.
26370.m: The Swiss Guard protects the Pope.

26371.q: Where does the Swiss Guard work?
26371.e: The Guard is based in the Vatican, the Pope’s small state in the middle of Rome.
26371.m: The Swiss Guard is in the Vatican.

26372.q: In which year was the Swiss Guard founded?
26372.e: Pope Julius II brought the first Swiss soldiers to Rome in 1506.
26372.m: The Swiss Guard has existed since 1506.

26373.q: Which long weapon do the guards carry on ceremonial occasions?
26373.e: The halberd is a long pole weapon with an axe blade and a point.

26374.q: What colours is the famous uniform of the Swiss Guard?
26374.e: The dress uniform has blue, yellow and red stripes.
26374.m: The Guard’s uniform is blue, yellow and red.

26375.q: On which day are new guards sworn in?
26375.e: On 6 May 1527 many guards died protecting the Pope. In memory of this, new guards take their oath on this day.
26375.m: New guards take their oath on 6 May.

26376.q: What nationality must a guard have?
26376.e: Only Swiss citizens may join the Swiss Guard.

26377.q: Which religion must a Swiss Guard belong to?
26377.e: Because the Guard protects the Pope, the guards must be Catholic.

26378.q: Why did Zurich join the Swiss Confederation in 1351?
a: It wanted to elect a king
It wanted to save on taxes
26378.e: Zurich had powerful enemies and looked for allies. So in 1351 Mayor Rudolf Brun made an alliance with the Confederates.
26378.m: In 1351 Zurich sought help against its enemies in the Confederation.

26379.q: Which two members joined the Confederation in 1352?
26379.e: In 1352 Glarus and Zug made alliances with the Confederates.

26380.q: What are the eight members called that formed the Confederation from 1353?
26380.e: Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden, Lucerne, Zurich, Glarus, Zug and Bern together are called the Eight Old Cantons.
26380.m: The first eight members are called the Eight Old Cantons.

26381.q: How many members did the Confederation have after Lucerne joined in 1332?
26381.e: Lucerne joined the three Forest Cantons as the fourth member.
26381.m: With Lucerne there were four members.

26382.q: With which members did Lucerne make its alliance in 1332?
26382.e: Lucerne allied itself with the three members on the lake that had already belonged together since 1291.
26382.m: Lucerne allied itself with Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden.

26383.q: Who ruled the town of Lucerne before it allied itself with the Confederates?
26383.e: At that time Lucerne belonged to the Habsburgs. Even so, the town made an alliance with the Forest Cantons in 1332.
26383.m: Lucerne used to be under Habsburg rule.

26384.q: In which period did Lucerne, Zurich and Bern join the Confederation?
26384.e: All three towns joined between 1332 and 1353, that is, in the 14th century.
26384.m: Lucerne, Zurich and Bern joined in the 14th century.

26385.q: Why did Bern joining matter so much for the Confederation?
a: Bern was a strong town with a lot of land
26385.e: Bern ruled a large territory and had many soldiers. This made the Confederation much stronger.
26385.m: With Bern the Confederation became much stronger.

26387.q: How many members did the Confederation have after two towns were admitted in 1481?
26387.e: In 1481 two new towns joined the eight old members. That makes ten members.
26387.m: From 1481 the Confederation had ten members.

26388.q: How many members did the Confederation have after the new members joined in 1501?
26388.e: In 1501 two more towns joined the ten members. That makes twelve members.
26388.m: From 1501 the Confederation had twelve members.

26389.q: What do you call areas that were allied with the Confederates but were not full members?
26389.e: Associates were friends and partners of the Confederation but did not have all the rights of full members.
26389.m: Allies without full rights were called associates.

26390.q: What is a member (“Ort”) of the old Swiss Confederation called today?
26390.e: The members of the old Confederation correspond to today’s cantons.
26390.m: The old members became the cantons.

26391.q: Which language was spoken in most of the thirteen members?
26391.e: Almost all thirteen members were German-speaking. Only in Fribourg did a large part of the people speak French.
26391.m: In the thirteen members people mostly spoke German.

26392.q: Which city did not belong to the thirteen members but was only allied with them?
26392.e: Geneva was an associate. It only became a full canton in 1815.
26392.m: Geneva only became a canton in 1815.

26393.q: Which present-day canton was a subject territory at the time of the thirteen members?
26393.e: From 1460 several members governed Thurgau jointly. It had no rights of its own in the Confederation.
26393.m: For a long time Thurgau remained a subject territory.

26394.q: In which city was Huldrych Zwingli the priest at the Grossmünster?
26394.e: From 1519 Zwingli preached at the Grossmünster in Zurich. From there his Reformation spread.
26394.m: Zwingli preached at the Grossmünster in Zurich.

26395.q: In which valley did Zwingli come into the world?
26395.e: Zwingli came into the world in 1484 in Wildhaus in the Toggenburg. You can still visit the house where he was born.
26395.m: Zwingli came from Wildhaus in the Toggenburg.

26396.q: What job did Huldrych Zwingli have?
26396.e: Zwingli was a priest and preacher. He wanted to renew the Church.
26396.m: Zwingli worked as a priest and reformer.

26397.q: What did Zwingli want to achieve with the Reformation?
26397.e: Reformation means renewal. Zwingli wanted the Church to follow the Bible again.

26398.q: What did Zwingli have removed from the churches in Zurich?
26398.e: Zwingli felt that pictures and statues of saints distracted people from prayer. So in 1524 they were removed from Zurich’s churches.
26398.m: Zwingli’s churches no longer had pictures of saints.

26399.q: What did Zwingli fight against because many young Swiss men died doing it?
26399.e: Many young Swiss men fought as mercenaries for foreign rulers and lost their lives. Zwingli had seen this himself as an army chaplain and was therefore against it.
26399.m: Zwingli opposed mercenary service for foreign rulers.

26400.q: Into which language was the Bible translated in Zurich under Zwingli?
26400.e: Zwingli and his helpers translated the Bible into German. This meant people could read it for themselves.
26400.m: The Zurich Bible is written in German.

26401.q: What is Zwingli holding in the monument by the Wasserkirche in Zurich?
26401.e: The Zwingli monument has stood by the Wasserkirche since 1885. It shows him with a Bible and a sword.
26401.m: The Zwingli monument shows him with a Bible and a sword.

26402.e: Zwingli went with the Zurich troops in the Second War of Kappel. He was killed at the Battle of Kappel am Albis.
26402.m: Zwingli died in 1531 at the Battle of Kappel.

26403.q: In which city did the reformer John Calvin work?
26403.e: Calvin lived and preached in Geneva for many years. He made the city a centre of the Reformation.
26403.m: Calvin was the reformer of Geneva.
