26404.q: What did Calvin actually plan to do when he came to Geneva in 1536?
26404.e: Calvin only wanted to stay one night. But the preacher Guillaume Farel persuaded him to stay in Geneva and help.

26405.q: What nickname did Geneva get because of Calvin?
26405.e: Geneva became as important for Protestants as Rome for Catholics. That is why people called it the “Protestant Rome”.
26405.m: Because of Calvin, Geneva got the name Protestant Rome.

26406.q: In which church in Geneva did Calvin preach?
26406.e: Calvin preached in St Peter’s Cathedral (Saint-Pierre) in Geneva’s Old Town. You can still see his chair there.
26406.m: Calvin preached in St Peter’s Cathedral.

26407.q: What did Calvin found in Geneva in 1559?
26407.e: Calvin founded the Geneva Academy in 1559. It later became the University of Geneva.
26407.m: Calvin’s academy later became the University of Geneva.

26408.q: What is the large monument in Geneva showing Calvin and other reformers called?
26408.e: The Reformation Wall stands in the Parc des Bastions. It is a long wall with large stone figures.
26408.m: The Reformation Wall in Geneva shows Calvin.

26409.q: What did Calvin have to do in 1538, only two years after he arrived?
26409.e: The Geneva council sent Calvin out of the city in 1538. In 1541 they brought him back.
26409.m: Calvin was banished from Geneva and later brought back.

26410.q: Until what year did Calvin live in Geneva?
26410.e: Calvin returned to Geneva in 1541 and stayed until his death in 1564.

26411.q: What did the men eat at the Zurich sausage meal of 1522?
26411.e: They ate smoked sausage even though it was Lent. At that time this broke the rules.
26411.m: At the sausage meal, people ate sausage during Lent.

26412.q: Why did the sausage meal of 1522 break the rules?
a: Because it took place at night
26412.e: During Lent before Easter, church rules said you could not eat meat. The men broke this rule on purpose.
26412.m: Eating meat during Lent broke the church rules.

26413.q: Where did the Zurich sausage meal take place?
26413.e: The sausage meal took place in the house of the printer Christoph Froschauer. His workers had a lot to do.
26413.m: The sausage meal took place at a printer’s.

26414.q: What did Zwingli do at the sausage meal?
a: He was there but did not eat
26414.e: Zwingli sat at the table but did not eat any sausage himself. Later he defended the others in a sermon.
26414.m: Zwingli attended the sausage meal but did not eat.

26415.q: In which year did the Zurich sausage meal take place?
26415.e: The sausage meal took place on 9 March 1522. It is seen as the start of the Reformation in Zurich.
26415.m: The sausage meal took place in 1522.

26416.q: Why is the sausage meal seen as important?
a: It marked a start of the Reformation
It marked the first festival in Zurich
26416.e: With the sausage meal, the open dispute about church rules began in Zurich. This led to the Zurich Reformation.
26416.m: The sausage meal set off the Reformation in Zurich.

26417.q: What was Zwingli’s sermon after the sausage meal about?
26417.e: Zwingli preached about freedom in what you eat. He said the Bible contains no rule about fasting.
26417.m: Zwingli preached that the Bible has no rule about fasting.

26418.q: What did Zurich decide about the fasting rules a few years after the sausage meal?
26418.e: In the following years the Reformation took hold in Zurich. After that the church fasting rules no longer applied; only the Bible was to count.

26419.q: Which animals did Thomas Platter look after as a little boy in Valais?
26419.e: Thomas Platter had to look after goats even as a small child. He later wrote about how hard this life was.
26419.m: As a child Thomas Platter looked after goats.

26420.q: What work did Thomas Platter do as a poor boy in Valais?
26420.e: Thomas Platter was a goatherd even as a small child. Later he learned to read and became a printer and teacher in Basel.
26420.m: As a child Thomas Platter was a goatherd.

26421.q: As what did Thomas Platter travel through foreign lands as a teenager?
26421.e: Platter wandered about for many years as a wandering scholar. He sang and begged to survive.
26421.m: Thomas Platter was a wandering scholar.

26422.q: Which craft did Thomas Platter learn in Zurich?
26422.e: Platter learned to twist ropes. On the side he worked hard at learning languages.
26422.m: Thomas Platter was also a rope-maker.

26423.q: In which city did Thomas Platter become a head teacher?
26423.e: For many years Platter ran the Latin school “auf Burg” in Basel. He died there in 1582.
26423.m: Thomas Platter became a head teacher in Basel.

26424.q: What did Thomas Platter write about his own life?
26424.e: Platter wrote the story of his life for his son Felix. That is why we know a lot about his childhood.
26424.m: Thomas Platter wrote down the story of his life.

26425.q: What job did Thomas Platter’s son Felix have?
26425.e: Felix Platter became a famous doctor in Basel. He also studied the human body closely.
26425.m: Felix Platter was a famous doctor.

26426.q: What did Thomas Platter run in Basel besides the school?
26426.e: Platter printed books in Basel together with others. One of them was an important book by Calvin.
26426.m: Thomas Platter printed books in Basel.

26427.q: Which city celebrates the Escalade every December?
26427.e: The Escalade is Geneva’s big festival. It recalls an attack in the year 1602.
26427.m: The Escalade is celebrated in Geneva.

26428.e: Duke Charles Emmanuel of Savoy wanted to conquer Geneva. His soldiers attacked at night.
26428.m: In the Escalade, Savoy attacked Geneva.

26429.q: What did the soldiers use to climb the Geneva city wall?
26429.e: The attackers put ladders against the wall. The word Escalade comes from the Latin word for ladder.
26429.m: Escalade means climbing a wall with ladders.

26430.q: At what time of day did the soldiers of Savoy attack Geneva?
26430.e: The attack took place during the night of 11 to 12 December 1602. The people of Geneva were to be surprised in their sleep.
26430.m: The Escalade was a night attack.

26431.q: What did Mère Royaume pour over a soldier?
26431.e: According to legend, Mère Royaume poured her pot of hot vegetable soup over an attacker. Then she threw the pot after it.
26431.m: Mère Royaume fought back with hot soup.

26432.q: What chocolate object do people smash at the Escalade?
26432.e: The chocolate pot is called a marmite. It recalls Mère Royaume’s soup pot.
26432.m: At the Escalade people smash a chocolate marmite.

26433.q: What is hidden inside the chocolate marmite of the Escalade?
26433.e: Inside the marmite are small marzipan vegetables. They recall the vegetable soup.
26433.m: The marmite is filled with marzipan vegetables.

26434.q: Who traditionally smashes the chocolate marmite?
26434.e: The youngest and the oldest person at the table hit the pot together. As they do so, they say a saying about the enemies of the Republic.
26434.m: Young and old smash the marmite together.

26435.q: How do children in Geneva celebrate the Escalade?
a: They throw confetti into the water
26435.e: At the Escalade many children walk through the streets in costume. There are also processions in historical costumes.
26435.m: Children dress up for the Escalade.

26436.e: Huguenots was the name for the Protestant Christians in France. They followed Calvin’s teaching.

26437.q: Why did many Huguenots flee from France?
a: Because of a war with Spain
26437.e: The King of France wanted to allow only the Catholic faith. The Huguenots were persecuted and fled.
26437.m: The Huguenots fled because of their faith.

26438.q: Which Swiss city did a particularly large number of Huguenots flee to?
26438.e: Geneva lies right on the border with France and was Protestant. That is why a great many refugees arrived there.

26439.q: Which king banned the Protestant faith in France in 1685?
26439.e: Louis XIV, the “Sun King”, cancelled the Edict of Nantes in 1685. After that tens of thousands of Huguenots fled.
26439.m: Louis XIV drove out the Huguenots.

26440.q: Which craft did Huguenots bring with them to Geneva?
26440.e: Among the refugees were skilled watchmakers and goldsmiths. They helped to make watchmaking big in Geneva.

26441.q: Where did many Huguenots move on to after a stop in Switzerland?
26441.e: Switzerland could not keep all the refugees. Many moved on, for example to Brandenburg and Hesse.
26441.m: Many Huguenots moved on from Switzerland to Germany.

26442.q: Where does the Huguenot and Waldensian Trail lead from southern France?
26442.e: The Huguenot and Waldensian Trail leads from southern France through Switzerland to Hesse in Germany. It follows the old escape routes.
26442.m: The Huguenot and Waldensian Trail recalls the Huguenots’ flight.

26443.q: Which language did the Huguenots speak?
26443.e: The Huguenots came from France and spoke French. In western Switzerland they were easily understood.

26444.q: In which Swiss mountain range is watchmaking especially at home?
26444.e: Many watchmaking workshops were set up in the Jura from the 18th century. Famous watch companies are still there today.
26444.m: The Jura is Switzerland’s watch country.

26445.q: When did farmers in the Jura use to work as watchmakers?
26445.e: In the long winter there was little work on the farm. So many farming families made watch parts in their living rooms.
26445.m: In winter, farmers in the Jura became watchmakers.

26446.q: What is the name of the young man who, according to legend, repaired an English watch in the Jura?
26446.e: Daniel JeanRichard is said to have repaired a broken watch from England as a teenager. Afterwards he made watches himself and trained apprentices.
26446.m: Daniel JeanRichard is seen as the father of watchmaking in the Jura.

26447.q: Which two watchmaking towns in the Jura are UNESCO World Heritage Sites?
26447.e: Both towns were built entirely for watchmakers. They have been UNESCO World Heritage Sites since 2009.
26447.m: La Chaux-de-Fonds and Le Locle are World Heritage watch towns.

26448.q: Why did watchmakers’ workshops use to have large windows?
a: For plenty of light while working
So you could see the mountains
26448.e: Watchmakers work with tiny parts. For this they needed a lot of daylight in their homes and workshops.
26448.m: Watchmakers need a lot of light.

26449.q: Which tool does a watchmaker need to see tiny parts?
26449.e: The parts of a watch are often smaller than a grain of rice. The magnifying glass makes them look big to the watchmaker.
26449.m: A watchmaker works with a magnifying glass.

26450.q: Which museum in La Chaux-de-Fonds shows watches and clocks from many centuries?
26450.e: The International Museum of Horology in La Chaux-de-Fonds shows thousands of watches and clocks. It is one of the largest watch museums in the world.
26450.m: There is a large watch museum in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

26451.q: What did UNESCO recognise in 2020 as the watchmaking art of Switzerland and France?
26451.e: UNESCO added watchmaking craftsmanship in the Jura Arc to the list of intangible cultural heritage. This means the knowledge and skills of the people.
26451.m: Watchmaking craftsmanship is intangible cultural heritage.

26452.q: Which valley in the Vaud Jura is known for fine watches?
26452.e: Watchmakers have worked in the Vallée de Joux for a long time. Especially complicated watches are made there.
26452.m: The Vallée de Joux is a watchmaking valley in the Jura.

26453.q: What did the Basel Paper Mill use to make?
26453.e: Paper was made by hand in the mill. Today it is a museum.
26453.m: Paper was made in the Basel Paper Mill.

26454.q: What drives the machines of the Basel Paper Mill?
26454.e: The mill stands on a canal, the St. Alban-Teich. The water turns a large wheel.
26454.m: A water wheel drives the paper mill.

26455.q: On which river is the Basel Paper Mill?
26455.e: The paper mill stands in the St. Alban-Tal, very close to the Rhine. A canal brings the water for the water wheel.
26455.m: The Basel Paper Mill is on the Rhine.

26456.q: What was paper made from in the past?
26456.e: Paper used to be made from rags of linen and hemp. The rags were pounded into a pulp.
26456.m: Old paper was made from cloth rags.

26457.q: What can children make themselves at the Basel Paper Mill?
26457.e: In the museum you can use a sieve to scoop a sheet of paper out of the pulp yourself. Afterwards you can even print on it.
26457.m: At the paper mill you can make paper yourself.

26458.q: What do you use to scoop paper out of the vat?
26458.e: The paper pulp floats in water. With a sieve you lift out a thin layer, which becomes a sheet.
26458.m: Paper is scooped with a sieve.

26459.q: What is the museum in the Basel Paper Mill called?
a: Museum of Paper, Writing and Printing
26459.e: The museum shows how paper is made, how people write and how books used to be printed.
26459.m: The paper mill is a museum of paper, writing and printing.

26460.q: What did the printers in Basel need a lot of paper for?
26460.e: Basel used to be an important city for printers. A lot of paper was needed for all those books.
26460.m: The Basel printers needed a lot of paper.

26461.e: Paracelsus was a doctor and natural scientist. He wanted to understand illnesses better.

26462.q: Near which Swiss place did Paracelsus come into the world?
26462.e: Paracelsus came into the world near Einsiedeln around 1493. His father also worked as a doctor there.

26463.q: Which famous saying of Paracelsus is about poison?
a: You can recognise poison by its smell
26463.e: Paracelsus taught that almost anything can be poisonous if you take too much of it. So it all depends on the amount.

26464.q: In which language did Paracelsus give his lectures in Basel?
26464.e: At that time professors taught in Latin. Paracelsus spoke German so that more people could understand him.
26464.m: Paracelsus taught in German instead of Latin.

26465.q: What did Paracelsus do especially often throughout his life?
26465.e: Paracelsus travelled through many countries in Europe. On the way he learned from doctors, miners and herb women.

26466.q: What did Paracelsus study to make medicines?
26466.e: Paracelsus made remedies from plants, but also from metals and minerals. This made him a pioneer.
26466.m: Paracelsus made remedies from plants and metals.

26467.q: In which city did Paracelsus die in 1541?
26467.e: Paracelsus died in 1541 in Salzburg in Austria. He is also buried there.

26468.q: In which Swiss city was Paracelsus the town doctor in 1527?
26468.e: In 1527 Paracelsus became town doctor and teacher in Basel. But he only stayed a short time because he had many quarrels.
26468.m: Paracelsus was briefly the town doctor in Basel.

26469.q: What was Conrad Gessner’s famous big book about?
26469.e: Gessner wrote a huge work about all the animals he knew. It is called “Historia animalium”.
26469.m: Conrad Gessner wrote a big book about animals.

26470.q: In which city did Conrad Gessner live?
26470.e: Gessner, born in Zurich in 1516, worked as the town doctor there. He also died in Zurich.

26471.q: How were the pictures in Gessner’s animal book printed?
26471.e: The pictures were carved into wooden blocks and then printed. This technique is called woodcut.

26472.q: Which mythical animal can also be found in Gessner’s animal book?
26472.e: Gessner also included animals that people only told stories about, for example the unicorn. At that time people did not yet know exactly which animals really existed.
26472.m: The unicorn also appears in Gessner’s animal book.

26473.q: Which animal in Gessner’s book is based on a picture by Albrecht Dürer?
26473.e: Gessner used Albrecht Dürer’s famous rhinoceros. Dürer himself had never seen the animal.
26473.m: Gessner’s rhinoceros comes from Albrecht Dürer.

26474.q: What job did Conrad Gessner have in Zurich?
26474.e: From 1554 Gessner was the town doctor in Zurich. Alongside this he studied animals and plants.
26474.m: Gessner was a doctor and natural scientist.

26475.q: Which mountain near Lucerne did Conrad Gessner climb in 1555?
26475.e: Gessner climbed Pilatus in 1555 and wrote about it. At that time only a few people climbed mountains for fun.

26476.q: What did Conrad Gessner die of in 1565?
26476.e: The plague was raging in Zurich in 1565. Gessner cared for the sick and caught it himself.
26476.m: Conrad Gessner died of the plague.

26477.q: In which city was Matthäus Merian born?
26477.e: Matthäus Merian was born in Basel in 1593. Later he lived in Frankfurt.

26478.q: What did Matthäus Merian especially like to draw?
26478.e: Merian made hundreds of pictures of towns. They show what the towns looked like almost 400 years ago.

26479.q: Which technique did Merian use to make his pictures?
26479.e: Merian engraved the pictures into copper plates. Many prints could be made from them.

26480.q: From what point of view did Merian show the city of Basel on his famous plan?
a: From the bank of the Rhine
26480.e: In 1615 Merian drew Basel as if he were flying over it at an angle like a bird. So you can see all the houses and streets.
26480.m: Merian drew Basel from a bird’s-eye view.

26481.q: In which German city did Merian run a publishing house?
26481.e: Merian married into a Frankfurt publishing family. There he published his books.

26482.q: What did Merian’s daughter Maria Sibylla become famous for?
26482.e: Maria Sibylla Merian painted caterpillars and butterflies very precisely. She even travelled to South America to do so.

26483.e: The “Topographia” is a large series of books with pictures and descriptions of towns and regions. There is also a volume about Switzerland.
26483.m: Merian’s Topographia describes countries and towns.

26484.q: Why are Merian’s pictures valuable to us today?
a: They show what towns used to look like
They are the oldest pictures of Switzerland
They are all painted in colour
26484.e: Many old houses and walls no longer exist today. You can still see them in Merian’s pictures.
26484.m: Merian’s pictures show what old towns looked like.

26485.q: What did the soldiers eat together at the Kappel milk soup?
26485.e: The soldiers sat around a big pot and ate milk soup together. Instead of fighting, they shared the food.
26485.m: At Kappel soldiers shared a milk soup.

26486.q: In which year did the Kappel milk soup take place?
26486.e: The milk soup happened in 1529 during the First War of Kappel. No battle took place.
26486.m: The Kappel milk soup took place in 1529.

26487.q: Who brought the bread for the Kappel milk soup?
26487.e: The Zurich troops had bread, the troops from Central Switzerland had milk. Together that made a soup.
26487.m: The people of Zurich brought the bread for the milk soup.

26488.q: Who brought the milk for the Kappel milk soup?
26488.e: The troops from Central Switzerland had milk. The Zurich troops brought the bread to go with it.
26488.m: The people of Central Switzerland brought the milk.

26489.q: Why did Zurich and Central Switzerland face each other as enemies in 1529?
26489.e: Zurich had become Protestant, while the cantons of Central Switzerland stayed Catholic. They fell out over this.
26489.m: The dispute at Kappel concerned religion.

26490.q: Where did the pot stand at the Kappel milk soup?
26490.e: The pot was placed exactly on the border between Zurich and Zug. Each side ate from its own side.
26490.m: The soup pot stood on the border.

26491.q: Which painter from Bern painted the Kappel milk soup in 1869?
26491.e: Albert Anker painted the scene of the soldiers sitting peacefully around the pot. The picture is very well known.
26491.m: Albert Anker painted the Kappel milk soup.

26492.q: What does the story of the Kappel milk soup show?
a: The people of Zurich were the strongest
The people of Central Switzerland had nothing to eat
The war lasted a very long time
26492.e: Instead of a battle there was a shared meal and a peace. The story is seen as a sign of the unity of the Confederates.
26492.m: The Kappel milk soup is a sign of peace.

26493.q: Which country sent soldiers into Switzerland in 1798?
26493.e: In 1798 French troops marched into Switzerland. This is called the French invasion.
26493.m: In 1798 French soldiers came to Switzerland.

26494.q: In which year did the French march into Switzerland?
26494.e: In spring 1798 French troops occupied Switzerland. That marked the end of the Old Swiss Confederation.

26495.q: Which big city fell into French hands in March 1798?
26495.e: On 5 March 1798 the Bernese lost against the French. After that the French entered the city of Bern.
26495.m: In March 1798 the French captured the city of Bern.

26496.q: What did the French take from Bern in 1798?
26496.e: The French took Bern’s rich state treasure. Among other things, they used the money to pay for their wars.
26496.m: The French stole Bern’s state treasure in 1798.

26497.q: What is the name of the place near Bern where a battle against the French took place in 1798?
26497.e: At Grauholz near Bern, the Bernese fought the French on 5 March 1798. They lost the battle.
26497.m: At Grauholz the Bernese lost to the French in 1798.

26498.q: Which canton fought back especially fiercely against the French in September 1798?
26498.e: The people of Nidwalden did not want to accept the new order. In September 1798 there was terrible fighting with many deaths.

26499.q: What came to an end with the French invasion of 1798?
26499.e: With the invasion of the French, the Old Swiss Confederation collapsed. After that a new state was created.
26499.m: The French invasion ended the Old Swiss Confederation.

26500.q: What was the new state that came into being in Switzerland in 1798 called?
26500.e: After the French invasion, the Helvetic Republic was founded in 1798. France had a strong say in it.
26500.m: The Helvetic Republic came into being in 1798.

26501.q: In which town was the Helvetic Republic proclaimed?
26501.e: The Helvetic Republic was proclaimed in Aarau on 12 April 1798. So Aarau became the first capital.
26501.m: The Helvetic Republic began in Aarau.

26502.q: What colours did the flag of the Helvetic Republic have?
26502.e: The Helvetic Republic had a flag with three stripes in green, red and yellow. The white cross on red only came back later.
26502.m: The Helvetic flag had green, red and yellow stripes.

26503.q: What was new in the Helvetic Republic?
26503.e: The Helvetic Republic brought equality before the law. There were no longer any subjects who had to obey other members.
26503.m: In the Helvetic Republic all citizens stood equal before the law.

26504.q: What were the cantons in the Helvetic Republic?
26504.e: The Helvetic Republic was a unitary state. The cantons could hardly decide anything for themselves any more.
26504.m: In the Helvetic Republic the cantons had little power.

26505.q: Until what year did the Helvetic Republic exist?
26505.e: The Helvetic Republic lasted from 1798 to 1803. Then Napoleon reorganised Switzerland.

26506.q: How many men led the government of the Helvetic Republic at first?
26506.e: The government was called the Directory and had five directors. This followed the French model.
26506.m: The Helvetic Directory had five members.

26507.q: What was the short uprising of 1802 against the Helvetic Republic called?
26507.e: In 1802 opponents of the Helvetic Republic often fought only with wooden sticks. That is why the uprising is called the War of the Sticks.
26507.m: The War of the Sticks in 1802 targeted the Helvetic Republic.

26508.q: Which subject territories existed in the Helvetic Republic?
26508.e: Before, some areas had to obey other members. The Helvetic Republic abolished these subject territories.
26508.m: The Helvetic Republic abolished the subject territories.

26509.q: What job did Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi do?
26509.e: Pestalozzi was a famous educator. He wanted all children to be able to learn well.
26509.m: Pestalozzi became a famous teacher and educator.

26510.q: In which city was Pestalozzi born in 1746?
26510.e: Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi came into the world in Zurich on 12 January 1746.

26511.q: According to Pestalozzi, with which three things should children learn?
26511.e: Pestalozzi said that you should learn with head, heart and hand. Thinking, feeling and doing belong together.
26511.m: According to Pestalozzi, you learn with head, heart and hand.

26512.q: Which children did Pestalozzi look after in Stans in 1799?
26512.e: After the fighting of 1798 there were many orphans there. Pestalozzi looked after them in Stans in 1799.
26512.m: Pestalozzi helped poor orphans in Stans.

26513.q: In which town on Lake Neuchâtel did Pestalozzi run a well-known institute from 1805?
26513.e: Pestalozzi ran an institute in Yverdon for about 20 years. Visitors from all over Europe came to see his school.
26513.m: Pestalozzi’s famous institute was in Yverdon.

26514.q: In which Bernese town did Pestalozzi teach in a castle from 1800?
26514.e: Pestalozzi taught in Burgdorf from 1800. There he opened a school in the castle.

26515.q: What is the title of a well-known book by Pestalozzi?
26515.e: Pestalozzi wrote the novel “Leonard and Gertrude”. It tells of the life of a simple family in the countryside.
26515.m: Pestalozzi wrote the book “Leonard and Gertrude”.

26516.q: What was the name of Pestalozzi’s farm in Aargau, where he took in poor children?
26516.e: At the Neuhof near Birr, Pestalozzi took in poor children. They worked and learned there together.
26516.m: Pestalozzi’s farm in Aargau had the name Neuhof.

26517.q: In which year did Pestalozzi die?
26517.e: Pestalozzi died in Brugg on 17 February 1827. He was buried in Birr.

26518.q: What is the period from 1803 to 1813 in Switzerland called?
26518.e: The period after the Act of Mediation is called the Mediation period. It ended in 1813, when Napoleon lost the war.
26518.m: The Mediation period lasted from 1803 to 1813.

26519.q: What is the law of 1803 that Napoleon gave Switzerland called?
26519.e: The Act of Mediation of 1803 got its name because Napoleon acted as a go-between. “Mediation” means helping two sides agree.
26519.m: In 1803 Switzerland received the Act of Mediation.

26520.q: Which of these cantons was newly founded in 1803?
26520.e: Aargau became a canton of its own in 1803. Uri, Zurich and Glarus had been members for much longer.
26520.m: Aargau has been a canton since 1803.

26521.q: Which canton in the south became a canton of its own in 1803?
26521.e: Ticino became a canton in 1803. Before that it had been a subject territory of the Confederates.
26521.m: Ticino became a canton of its own in 1803.

26522.q: Which canton on Lake Constance was newly founded in 1803?
26522.e: Thurgau became a canton of its own in 1803. Before that the Confederates had governed it jointly.
26522.m: Thurgau has been a canton since 1803.

26523.q: Which canton on Lake Geneva became a canton of its own in 1803?
26523.e: Vaud used to belong to Bern. In 1803 it became a canton of its own.

26524.q: Which large mountain canton joined Switzerland in 1803?
26524.e: Before, the Grisons had only been allied with the Confederates. In 1803 it became a proper canton.
26524.m: The Grisons has been a Swiss canton since 1803.

26525.q: How many cantons did Switzerland have after 1803?
26525.e: In 1803 six new cantons joined the 13 old members. That makes 19 cantons.

26526.q: In which city did the rulers of Europe meet in 1814 and 1815?
26526.e: After Napoleon’s defeat, the powers of Europe met in Vienna. This meeting is called the Congress of Vienna.
26526.m: The Congress of Vienna took place in Vienna.

26527.q: Which treaty joined the cantons together from 1815?
26527.e: In 1815 the cantons made the Federal Treaty. It remained in force until the federal state was founded.
26527.m: From 1815 the Federal Treaty applied between the cantons.

26528.q: What does it mean if a country is neutral?
a: It does not take part in wars
26528.e: A neutral country does not fight in other countries’ wars. It also does not help either side with soldiers.
26528.m: A neutral country stays out of wars.

26529.q: Which city on Lake Geneva became a Swiss canton in 1815?
26529.e: Geneva became a Swiss canton in 1815. Before that France had occupied the city.
26529.m: Geneva has been a Swiss canton since 1815.

26530.q: Which mountain canton with the Matterhorn joined Switzerland in 1815?
26530.e: Valais became a Swiss canton in 1815. The famous Matterhorn is also there.
26530.m: Valais has belonged to Switzerland since 1815.

26531.q: Which canton in the Jura area with many watchmakers joined in 1815?
26531.e: Neuchâtel became a Swiss canton in 1815. The canton of Jura only came into being much later, in 1979.
26531.m: Neuchâtel has been a Swiss canton since 1815.

26532.q: How many cantons did Switzerland have after 1815?
26532.e: In 1815 three more joined the 19 cantons. That made 22 cantons.

26533.q: Who had lost the war in Europe before the Congress of Vienna?
26533.e: Napoleon was defeated in 1814 by Russia, Austria, Prussia and other countries. Afterwards the winners reorganised Europe.
26533.m: After Napoleon’s defeat the Congress of Vienna reorganised Europe.

26534.q: Which area did the canton of Bern receive in 1815 to make up for losing Vaud?
26534.e: The Congress of Vienna gave Bern the area of the former Prince-Bishopric of Basel in the Jura. This compensated Bern for the loss of Vaud.
26534.m: In 1815 the Jura became part of the canton of Bern.

26535.q: In which year was the Swiss federal state founded?
26535.e: In 1848 Switzerland got a new Federal Constitution. This created the modern federal state.
26535.m: The Swiss federal state came into being in 1848.

26536.e: Before 1848 the cantons were only loosely connected. Only the Federal Constitution turned this into a federal state.
26536.m: Before 1848 Switzerland formed a loose confederation of states.

26537.q: Which short war took place shortly before the federal state was founded?
26537.e: In 1847 liberal and Catholic conservative cantons fought in the Sonderbund War.
26537.m: The Sonderbund War of 1847 came before the federal state.

26538.q: What was the assembly of the cantons called before 1848?
26538.e: Before 1848 envoys of the cantons met at the Diet. With the federal state it was replaced by Parliament.
26538.m: Before 1848 the cantons held discussions at the Diet.

26540.q: What could Swiss men do throughout the country from 1848?
a: Only stay in their home canton
26540.e: The Federal Constitution of 1848 allowed Swiss citizens to settle in any canton. At first, however, this only applied to Christians; Jewish Swiss only received this right in 1866.
26540.m: From 1848 Swiss people could settle in any canton.

26542.q: Who became responsible for the post after the federal state was founded?
26542.e: The Federal Constitution of 1848 made the post a matter for the Confederation. Before that the cantons had their own postal services.
26542.m: Since the founding of the federal state, the post has been a matter for the Confederation.

26543.q: What is the Federal Palace in Bern?
a: The seat of government and parliament
26543.e: Parliament and the Federal Council meet in the Federal Palace. This is where Switzerland is governed.
26543.m: The government and parliament work in the Federal Palace.

26544.q: In which year was today’s Parliament Building opened?
26544.e: The Parliament Building opened on 1 April 1902. Its construction lasted from 1894 to 1902.

26545.q: In which city is the Federal Palace?
26545.e: The Federal Palace is in Bern. Parliament and the Federal Council work there.
26545.m: The Federal Palace is in Bern.

26546.q: What is right at the top of the dome of the Federal Palace?
26546.e: On top of the green dome there is a gilded Swiss cross. It is around 60 metres above the ground.
26546.m: A golden cross shines on the dome of the Federal Palace.

26547.q: What colour is the dome of the Federal Palace?
26547.e: The dome is covered with copper. Over time the copper turned green.
26547.m: The dome of the Federal Palace is green.

26548.q: Which three men does the large statue in the hall of the Federal Palace show?
26548.e: The three Confederates of the Rütli oath stand in the domed hall. The statue was unveiled in 1914.
26548.m: The three Confederates stand as a statue in the Federal Palace.

26549.q: How many water fountains spray on the Federal Square in front of the Federal Palace?
26549.e: There are 26 water jets on the Federal Square. Each one stands for a canton.
26549.m: The 26 fountains on the Federal Square stand for the cantons.

26550.q: Where do the stones used to build the Parliament Building come from?
26550.e: Around 30 kinds of stone from 13 cantons were used in the building. So the building shows the variety of Switzerland.
26550.m: The Federal Palace contains stones from many cantons.

26551.q: What are the covered walkways in Bern’s Old Town called?
26551.e: Bern’s Old Town has kilometres of arcades. You can go shopping there and stay dry even in the rain.
26551.m: In Bern you can walk through the Old Town under the arcades and stay dry.

26552.q: In which year was Bern chosen as the federal city?
26552.e: On 28 November 1848 Parliament chose Bern as the seat of the federal authorities.
26552.m: Bern became the federal city in 1848.

26553.q: Which other city also wanted to become the federal city in 1848?
26553.e: Zurich and Lucerne also wanted to become the federal city. But Parliament chose Bern.
26553.m: In 1848 Bern won against Zurich and Lucerne.

26554.q: Why do people often call Bern the “federal city” rather than the “capital”?
a: Bern is too small for a capital
26554.e: According to the constitution, Switzerland has no official capital. Bern is the seat of the federal authorities and is therefore called the federal city.
26554.m: Officially Bern is the federal city, not the capital.

26555.q: Which church in Bern has the tallest church tower in Switzerland?
a: The Church of the Holy Spirit
26555.e: The tower of Bern Minster is around 100 metres high. No other church tower in Switzerland is taller.
26555.m: Bern Minster has the tallest church tower in Switzerland.

26556.q: Which city has more inhabitants than the federal city of Bern?
26556.e: Zurich is the largest city in Switzerland. Bern is the federal city, but it has fewer inhabitants.
26556.m: The federal city of Bern is smaller than Zurich.

26557.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the federal city of Bern?
26557.e: In Bern people mainly speak German, and in everyday life Bernese German. But the canton of Bern is bilingual.
26557.m: In Bern people mainly speak Bernese German.

26558.q: What rank did Henri Dufour hold in the Sonderbund War of 1847?
26558.e: In 1847 Dufour led the troops of the Diet as general. He wanted as few victims as possible.
26558.m: Henri Dufour served as general in the Sonderbund War.

26559.q: What did General Dufour have made for the whole of Switzerland for the first time?
26559.e: Under Dufour’s direction the first accurate map of the whole of Switzerland was made. It is called the Dufour Map.
26559.m: The Dufour Map is named after General Dufour.

26561.q: In which city did Henri Dufour live and die?
26561.e: Dufour lived and worked mainly in Geneva. He died there in 1875.

26562.q: Which aid organisation did Dufour help to found?
26562.e: In 1863 Dufour was one of the founders of the committee that became the Red Cross. He worked with Henry Dunant on it.
26562.m: Dufour helped to found the Red Cross.

26563.q: What is the scale of the Dufour Map?
26563.e: The Dufour Map has a scale of 1 to 100,000. So one centimetre on the map is one kilometre in real life.
26563.m: On the Dufour Map one centimetre is one kilometre.

26564.q: How does the Dufour Map show the mountains so vividly?
a: With shading as if lit by light
With one colour for each height
With small drawn pictures of mountains
26564.e: The Dufour Map shows mountains with hatching and shading, as if light were falling on them. This makes the mountains look almost three-dimensional.
26564.m: The Dufour Map shows mountains with shading.

26565.q: Roughly how long did the Sonderbund War under General Dufour last?
26565.e: The Sonderbund War in November 1847 lasted only about four weeks. Dufour made sure there were few deaths.
26565.m: The Sonderbund War lasted only a short time.

26567.q: How many centimes (Rappen) are there in a franc?
26567.e: A franc is divided into 100 centimes. It has been like this since 1850.

26568.q: What was money like in Switzerland before the franc?
a: Everyone paid with Spanish gold coins
26568.e: Before 1850 cantons and towns had their own coins. That made paying complicated.
26568.m: Before 1850 there were many different coins in Switzerland.

26569.q: Which female figure can you see on many Swiss coins?
26569.e: Helvetia is the female figure who represents Switzerland. You can see her on the franc coins, for example.

26570.q: What is the five-franc coin called in everyday Swiss speech?
26570.e: In Swiss German dialect the large five-franc coin is called a Fünfliber. It shows a herdsman.
26570.m: The five-franc coin is called a Fünfliber.

26571.q: What is the international abbreviation for the Swiss franc?
26571.e: The abbreviation CHF stands for Confoederatio Helvetica Franc. It is used all over the world.
26571.m: The Swiss franc is abbreviated to CHF.

26572.q: In which city are Swiss coins minted today?
26572.e: The Federal Mint, Swissmint, is based in Bern. The coins are made there.
26572.m: Swiss coins are minted in Bern.

26573.q: Which law brought the franc to the whole of Switzerland in 1850?
26573.e: The first federal law on coinage, from 1850, introduced the franc. Only the federal state made a common currency possible.
26573.m: The Coinage Act of 1850 introduced the franc.

26574.q: Who painted the famous picture “The Gotthard Post”?
26574.e: The Zurich painter Rudolf Koller painted the Gotthard Post in 1873. He was known for his pictures of animals.
26574.m: Rudolf Koller painted the Gotthard Post.

26575.q: How many horses pull the coach in the picture “The Gotthard Post”?
26575.e: The coach is pulled by five horses, so it is called a five-horse coach. Three greys run in front, two browns behind.
26575.m: The Gotthard Post is a five-horse coach.

26576.q: Which animal runs in fright in front of the coach in the picture “The Gotthard Post”?
26576.e: A calf runs away in panic in front of the coach. Next to it there is a herd of cows on the road.
26576.m: In the Gotthard Post a calf runs in front of the coach.

26577.q: On which winding pass road is the coach travelling in the picture?
26577.e: Koller painted the south side of the Gotthard, where the Tremola leads down towards Airolo with many tight bends. But he put the landscape in the picture together freely.
26577.m: The Gotthard Post travels on the Tremola.

26578.q: In which museum does the picture “The Gotthard Post” hang?
a: Swiss Museum of Transport in Lucerne
26578.e: The picture hangs in the Kunsthaus Zurich. It came there as a gift in 1898.
26578.m: The Gotthard Post hangs in the Kunsthaus Zurich.

26579.q: What brought an end to the regular stagecoaches over the Gotthard in 1882?
26579.e: In 1882 the Gotthard railway tunnel opened. After that people travelled by train instead of by coach.
26579.m: The Gotthard Tunnel of 1882 brought the end of the stagecoaches.

26580.q: Who received the picture “The Gotthard Post” as a farewell present?
26580.e: The North Eastern Railway gave the picture to Alfred Escher as a farewell present. Escher was an important supporter of the Gotthard Railway.
26580.m: The Gotthard Post was a present for Alfred Escher.

26581.q: What did the Gotthard Post carry over the pass besides travellers?
26581.e: The stagecoach carried travellers and the post. It connected the north side with Ticino.
26581.m: The Gotthard Post carried travellers and post over the pass.

26582.q: What shape is the Swiss flag?
26582.e: The Swiss flag is square. This is very rare for national flags.

26583.q: What can you see on the Swiss flag?
26583.e: The Swiss flag shows a white cross on a red background. The red cross on white is the symbol of the Red Cross.
26583.m: The Swiss flag shows a white cross on red.

26584.q: Which canton probably gave the Swiss flag its red?
26584.e: The red goes back mainly to the red flag of Schwyz. The name Switzerland also comes from Schwyz.
26584.m: The red of the Swiss flag comes from Schwyz.

26585.q: What shape is the Swiss flag on ships at sea?
26585.e: Swiss ocean-going ships sail under a rectangular flag. On land the flag is square.
26585.m: On ocean-going ships the Swiss flag is rectangular.

26586.q: What is true of the arms of the Swiss cross?
a: They are a little longer than they are wide
26586.e: Since 1889 it has been laid down that the arms are one sixth longer than they are wide. All four arms are the same length.
26586.m: The arms of the cross are a little longer than they are wide.

26587.q: Since when has the Swiss cross been the official coat of arms of the Confederation?
26587.e: In 1815 the white cross on a red field became the coat of arms of the Confederation. The federal state adopted the flag in 1848.
26587.m: The Swiss cross has been the coat of arms of the Confederation since 1815.

26588.q: Which organisation uses the reversed colours of the Swiss flag?
26588.e: The Red Cross honours Switzerland with a red cross on white. It was founded in Geneva.
26588.m: The Red Cross symbol is the Swiss flag reversed.

26589.q: On which holiday are especially many Swiss flags hung out?
26589.e: On 1 August Switzerland celebrates its national day. Then many people decorate their houses with flags.
26589.m: On 1 August Swiss flags hang everywhere.

26590.e: The Swiss National Bank has issued the banknotes since 1907. It makes sure that the franc stays stable.
26590.m: The National Bank issues Swiss banknotes.

26591.q: Which two towns did the Spanish Bun Railway connect?
26591.e: From 1847 the Spanish Bun Railway (Spanisch-Brötli-Bahn) ran from Zurich to Baden in Aargau.
26591.m: The Spanish Bun Railway ran from Zurich to Baden.

26592.q: In which year did the Spanish Bun Railway run for the first time?
26592.e: The first official train ran on 7 August 1847. From 9 August the railway ran to a timetable.
26592.m: The Spanish Bun Railway ran from 1847.

26593.q: What is the Spanish Bun Railway known for in Swiss history?
26593.e: It was the first railway line that lay entirely on Swiss soil.
26593.m: The first railway line entirely in Switzerland ran from Zurich to Baden.

26594.q: Where does the Spanish Bun Railway get its name from?
a: From a train driver from Spain
26594.e: Spanischbrötli were a fine pastry from Baden. Thanks to the railway they arrived fresh in Zurich.
26594.m: The railway is named after a pastry from Baden.

26595.q: What pulled the carriages of the Spanish Bun Railway?
26595.e: The trains were pulled by steam locomotives. At that time there was no electricity for railways yet.
26595.m: The first trains in Switzerland ran on steam.

26596.q: Roughly how long did the journey on the Spanish Bun Railway take?
26596.e: According to the timetable, the train took about three quarters of an hour for the good 20 kilometres.
26596.m: The journey from Zurich to Baden took about 45 minutes at that time.

26597.q: What was the name of the first locomotive, a replica of which still runs today?
26597.e: The locomotive bore the name “Limmat”, like the river in Zurich. A replica still runs on special occasions.
26597.m: The locomotive of the Spanish Bun Railway had the name Limmat.

26598.q: What was the Gotthard Tunnel when it opened in 1882?
a: The longest railway tunnel in the world
The first road tunnel in Switzerland
26598.e: At around 15 kilometres, the Gotthard Tunnel of 1882 held the record as the longest railway tunnel in the world. Only the Simplon Tunnel beat it.
26598.m: In 1882 the Gotthard Tunnel held the record as the longest railway tunnel in the world.

26599.q: In which year did the Gotthard railway tunnel open?
26599.e: After ten years of construction, the tunnel opened in 1882.
26599.m: The Gotthard railway tunnel opened in 1882.

26600.q: Which two places does the old Gotthard Tunnel connect?
26600.e: The tunnel begins in Göschenen in the canton of Uri and ends in Airolo in Ticino.
26600.m: The old Gotthard Tunnel runs from Göschenen to Airolo.

26601.q: Roughly how long is the Gotthard railway tunnel of 1882?
26601.e: The tunnel is around 15 kilometres long. At that time it held the record as the longest tunnel in the world.
26601.m: The old Gotthard Tunnel is about 15 kilometres long.

26602.q: Which country did most of the workers on the Gotthard Tunnel come from?
26602.e: Most of the tunnel workers came from Italy. They worked in very harsh conditions.
26602.m: Many Italians built the Gotthard Tunnel.

26603.q: Which two parts of the country did the Gotthard Tunnel connect better?
26603.e: Through the tunnel you could travel quickly by train from German-speaking Switzerland to Ticino and on to Italy.
26603.m: The Gotthard Tunnel connects the north with Ticino.

26604.q: What did they use to blast the rock when building the Gotthard Tunnel?
26604.e: With dynamite, which was new at the time, they could blast the hard rock.
26604.m: At the Gotthard they blasted the rock with dynamite.

26605.q: What was Louis Favre’s job on the Gotthard Tunnel?
26605.e: Louis Favre was the building contractor who led the construction of the tunnel.
26605.m: Louis Favre led the construction of the Gotthard Tunnel.

26606.q: Which part of Switzerland did Louis Favre come from?
26606.e: Louis Favre came from Chêne-Bourg near Geneva.
26606.m: Louis Favre came from the Geneva area.

26607.q: What happened to Louis Favre during the building of the tunnel?
a: He rode through on the first train
He built a second tunnel afterwards
26607.e: Louis Favre felt unwell during an inspection in the tunnel and died shortly afterwards of heart failure. He did not live to see the end of the work.
26607.m: Louis Favre died in the tunnel before it was finished.

26608.q: Which tunnel did Louis Favre build?
26608.e: Louis Favre from Geneva led the building of the Gotthard railway tunnel from 1872. He died in the tunnel in 1879, before the breakthrough.
26608.m: Louis Favre built the Gotthard Tunnel.

26609.q: What job did Louis Favre have?
26609.e: Louis Favre worked as a building contractor and had already built other tunnels.
26609.m: Louis Favre worked as a building contractor.

26610.q: When did the two construction teams meet in the Gotthard Tunnel?
26610.e: On 29 February 1880 the workers from the north and the south met inside the mountain. Louis Favre did not live to see it.
26610.m: The breakthrough at the Gotthard came in 1880.

26611.q: Which city did Alfred Escher come from?
26611.e: Alfred Escher was born in Zurich in 1819 and also died there in 1882.

26612.q: Which major building project did Alfred Escher campaign for?
26612.e: He was the most important supporter of the Gotthard Railway and headed the Gotthard Railway Company.
26612.m: Alfred Escher fought for the Gotthard Railway.

26613.q: Where in Zurich is the monument to Alfred Escher?
a: In front of the main station
26613.e: His statue stands on the station square in front of Zurich main station.
26613.m: A monument to Alfred Escher stands in front of Zurich main station.

26614.q: What kind of company did Alfred Escher found in 1856?
26614.e: He founded the Schweizerische Kreditanstalt, a bank, so as to have money for railways.
26614.m: Alfred Escher founded a bank for railway building.

26615.q: Which university did Alfred Escher help to found?
26615.e: Escher campaigned for the founding of ETH in Zurich. It opened in 1855.
26615.m: Alfred Escher helped to found ETH.

26616.q: Besides being a businessman, what else was Alfred Escher?
26616.e: Escher sat for many years in the National Council and in the Zurich government. He ranked among the most powerful politicians in Switzerland.
26616.m: Alfred Escher also played an important role in politics.

26617.q: What else did Alfred Escher build up besides banks?
26617.e: He headed the North Eastern Railway and drove forward railway building in Switzerland, for example the Gotthard Railway.
26617.m: Alfred Escher was a great railway pioneer.

26618.q: What do you call a railway that climbs steep mountains with a cogwheel?
26618.e: A cogwheel grips a toothed rail between the tracks. This stops the train from slipping on the steep slope.
26618.m: A rack railway climbs steep mountains with a cogwheel.

26619.q: Which mountain does the Vitznau-Rigi Railway go up?
26619.e: The railway runs from Vitznau on Lake Lucerne up the Rigi.
26619.m: The Vitznau-Rigi Railway goes up the Rigi.

26620.q: In which year did the Rigi Railway run for the first time?
26620.m: The Rigi Railway has been running since 1871.

26621.q: What is the Rigi Railway known for in Europe?
26621.e: The Rigi Railway became the first mountain railway in Europe.
26621.m: The Rigi Railway is the oldest mountain railway in Europe.

26622.e: The engineer Niklaus Riggenbach had invented a system with a toothed rack and used it to build the Rigi Railway.
26622.m: Niklaus Riggenbach built the Rigi Railway.

26623.q: On which lake is the Rigi?
26623.e: The Rigi stands between Lake Lucerne and Lake Zug.
26623.m: The Rigi is on Lake Lucerne.

26624.q: What lies between the rails of a rack railway?
26624.e: In the middle there is a toothed rack. The locomotive’s cogwheel grips into it.
26624.m: On a rack railway there is a toothed rack in the middle.

26625.q: What is the highest railway station in Europe called?
26625.e: Jungfraujoch station lies at 3,454 metres above sea level.
26625.m: The highest railway station in Europe is the Jungfraujoch.

26626.q: In which year did the Jungfrau Railway reach the Jungfraujoch?
26626.e: On 1 August 1912 the railway ran all the way to the Jungfraujoch for the first time.
26626.m: The Jungfrau Railway has gone up to the Jungfraujoch since 1912.

26627.q: Who had the idea for the Jungfrau Railway?
26627.e: The Zurich businessman Adolf Guyer-Zeller planned the railway from 1893.
26627.m: Adolf Guyer-Zeller had the idea for the Jungfrau Railway.

26628.q: Where does most of the Jungfrau Railway run?
26628.e: The railway mostly runs up through the Eiger and the Mönch in a tunnel.
26628.m: The Jungfrau Railway mostly runs through the mountain in a tunnel.

26629.q: Where does the Jungfrau Railway start?
26629.e: The Jungfrau Railway starts at Kleine Scheidegg and runs up to the Jungfraujoch. Other railways go to Grindelwald and Lauterbrunnen.
26629.m: The Jungfrau Railway starts at Kleine Scheidegg.

26630.q: In which region is the Jungfrau?
26630.e: The Jungfrau is one of the well-known mountains in the Bernese Oberland, along with the Eiger.
26630.m: The Jungfrau stands in the Bernese Oberland.

26631.q: In the 19th century, which country did many rich tourists come to Switzerland from?
26631.e: A particularly large number of guests came from England. They loved the mountains and the lakes.
26631.m: In the 19th century many English tourists came to Switzerland.

26632.q: What do you call a large, magnificent hotel like the ones built for tourists over 100 years ago?
26632.e: Grand hotels were huge, beautiful hotels with many rooms and halls.
26632.m: A large, elegant hotel is called a grand hotel.

26633.q: Why did more and more tourists come to Switzerland in the 19th century?
26633.e: With the railway, people could travel much faster and more comfortably.
26633.m: The railway brought many tourists to Switzerland.

26634.q: What did the early tourists in Switzerland mainly want to see?
26634.e: The guests admired the Alps, the glaciers and the clear lakes.
26634.m: The first tourists came for the mountains and lakes.

26635.q: In which place in the Grisons did winter tourism begin around 1864?
26635.e: The hotel owner Johannes Badrutt invited English guests to come to St Moritz in winter. They liked staying there.
26635.m: Winter tourism began in St Moritz.

26636.q: Where did the first electric light in Switzerland shine in 1879?
a: In a hotel in St Moritz
In the Federal Palace in Bern
26636.e: Johannes Badrutt had electric light put into the dining room of his Hotel Kulm in St Moritz.
26636.m: The first electric light in Switzerland shone in a hotel in St Moritz.

26637.q: Which Englishman organised the first group tour to Switzerland in 1863?
26637.e: Thomas Cook led a tour group through Switzerland in 1863. This marked the beginning of package tourism.
26637.m: Thomas Cook brought the first tour group to Switzerland.

26638.q: How did tourists usually travel over the Alps before the railway?
26638.e: Before the railway, travellers crossed the passes in coaches.
26638.m: In the past people crossed the Alps by coach.

26639.q: Which book did tourists take with them to know what there was to see on their journey?
26639.e: A guidebook contains routes, hotels and sights. Many tourists carried such a book with them.
26639.m: A guidebook shows what you can see on a journey.

26641.q: In which year was the Matterhorn climbed for the first time?
26641.e: On 14 July 1865 the first people stood on the summit.
26641.m: The Matterhorn was first climbed in 1865.

26642.q: Who led the first ascent of the Matterhorn?
26642.e: The Englishman Edward Whymper led the group to the summit.
26642.m: Edward Whymper climbed the Matterhorn first.

26643.q: Which country did Edward Whymper come from?
26643.e: Edward Whymper was an English illustrator and mountaineer.

26644.q: In which village at the foot of the Matterhorn did the first ascent begin?
26644.e: The group set off from the village of Zermatt in Valais.
26644.m: The first ascent of the Matterhorn began in Zermatt.

26645.q: What happened as the first climbers of the Matterhorn came down?
a: Four men fell to their deaths
They got lost in the fog
A thunderstorm trapped them for two days
26645.e: On the way down a rope broke. Four of the seven climbers fell into the depths.
26645.m: The first ascent of the Matterhorn ended in a terrible accident.

26646.e: Daniel Peter was the first to mix milk into chocolate.

26647.q: In which year did Daniel Peter invent milk chocolate?
26647.e: After many attempts he made the first milk chocolate in 1875.

26648.q: In which town on Lake Geneva did Daniel Peter work?
26648.e: Daniel Peter lived and worked in Vevey on Lake Geneva.

26649.q: What kind of milk did Daniel Peter use for his chocolate?
26649.e: Fresh milk contains a lot of water and goes off quickly. It worked with thickened condensed milk.
26649.m: Daniel Peter used condensed milk for milk chocolate.

26650.q: What did Daniel Peter make before he made chocolate?
26650.e: Daniel Peter first worked in candle-making.
26650.m: Daniel Peter started out as a candle-maker.

26651.q: Which famous neighbour supplied Daniel Peter with condensed milk?
26651.e: Henri Nestlé lived in the same town and made milk products.
26651.m: Daniel Peter and Henri Nestlé were neighbours.

26652.q: In which city did Rodolphe Lindt have his chocolate factory?
26652.e: Rodolphe Lindt opened a small factory in the Matte district of Bern in 1879.
26652.m: Rodolphe Lindt made chocolate in Bern.

26653.q: What did Rodolphe Lindt invent in 1879?
26653.e: Lindt invented a machine that stirs the chocolate mixture for a long time. This is called conching.

26654.q: What did the long stirring do to Lindt’s chocolate?
26654.e: Thanks to the long stirring, the chocolate becomes fine and melts in your mouth.
26654.m: Chocolate stirred for a long time is smooth and melting.

26655.q: What does a conche do with the chocolate mixture?
a: It stirs it for a long time
26655.e: The conche stirs and grinds the warm mixture for many hours.
26655.m: In the conche, chocolate is stirred for a long time.

26656.q: Where does the conche get its name from?
26656.e: The machine looked like a shell. The Spanish word for shell is “concha”.
26656.m: The conche is named after its shell shape.

26657.q: Which Zurich company did Lindt join up with in 1899?
26657.e: In 1899 Johann Rudolf Sprüngli bought Lindt’s factory. This is how Lindt & Sprüngli came about.
26657.m: Lindt and Sprüngli have belonged together since 1899.

26658.q: What was Rodolphe Lindt’s new chocolate called?
26658.e: Because it melted on the tongue, people called it melting chocolate.
26658.m: Lindt’s chocolate had the name melting chocolate.

26659.q: In which country was Henri Nestlé born?
26659.e: Henri Nestlé’s real name was Heinrich Nestle, and he came from Frankfurt am Main.

26660.q: What did Henri Nestlé invent for babies?
a: A baby food made from flour
26660.e: Nestlé developed a milk powder with cereal for infants, known as infant flour.
26660.m: Henri Nestlé invented an infant food for babies.

26661.q: What job had Henri Nestlé trained for?
26661.e: Henri Nestlé was a trained pharmacist and knew a lot about mixtures.
26661.m: Henri Nestlé worked as a pharmacist.

26662.q: What does the Nestlé logo show?
26662.e: In his dialect the name Nestlé means “little nest”. That is why the logo shows a nest with birds.
26662.m: The Nestlé logo is a bird’s nest.

26663.q: In which town did Henri Nestlé found his company?
26663.e: Henri Nestlé lived and worked in Vevey on Lake Geneva.
26663.m: The Nestlé company began in Vevey.

26664.q: Around which year did Henri Nestlé’s infant food come on the market?
26664.e: Henri Nestlé developed his infant food in 1866 and 1867.
26664.m: Henri Nestlé sold his infant food from about 1867.

26665.q: Which problem did Henri Nestlé want to help with his infant food?
a: Many babies did not get good food
26665.e: At that time many infants died because they did not get enough good food. The infant food was meant to help them.
26665.m: Henri Nestlé wanted to help babies with good food.

26666.e: The small company grew into one of the largest food companies in the world.
26666.m: Today Nestlé is a huge food company.

26667.q: What was the name of the inventor of Maggi products?
26667.e: Julius Maggi from Frauenfeld founded the Maggi company.
26667.m: Julius Maggi invented the Maggi products.

26668.q: In which canton did the large Maggi factory stand?
26668.e: Julius Maggi’s factory stood in Kemptthal near Winterthur in the canton of Zurich.
26668.m: The Maggi factory stood in the canton of Zurich.

26669.q: What did Julius Maggi invent in 1908?
26669.e: The Maggi stock cube came on the market in 1908. You dissolve it in hot water.
26669.m: Julius Maggi brought out the stock cube in 1908.

26670.q: What do you do with a stock cube?
a: You dissolve it in hot water
You eat it like a sweet
You bake it in the oven
26670.e: The cube dissolves in hot water and makes a broth.
26670.m: A stock cube dissolves in hot water.

26671.q: Who did Julius Maggi want to make cheap, nourishing soups for?
26671.e: Factory workers had little time and money. Maggi wanted to give them quick, healthy food.
26671.m: Maggi wanted to give workers quick food.

26672.q: What did Julius Maggi make his first soup powders from?
26672.e: He used flour made from peas, beans and lentils. These pulses are rich in protein.
26672.m: Maggi’s first soups were made from peas, beans and lentils.

26673.q: In which town in Thurgau was Julius Maggi born?
26673.e: Julius Maggi was born in Frauenfeld in 1846.

26674.q: What does the well-known bottle of Maggi seasoning look like?
a: Brown with a yellow and red label
26674.e: Since 1886 Maggi seasoning has come in a brown bottle with a yellow and red label.
26674.m: Maggi seasoning comes in a brown bottle.

a: A pattern made of threads on cloth
26675.e: In embroidery, patterns are sewn onto cloth with a needle and thread.
26675.m: Embroidery is a pattern made of threads on cloth.

26676.q: Which city does the famous embroidery of eastern Switzerland come from?
26676.e: Eastern Switzerland around St Gallen was world-famous for fine embroidery.
26676.m: St Gallen is famous for its embroidery.

26677.q: What greatly changed embroidery in eastern Switzerland in the 19th century?
26677.e: At first embroidery was done by hand, then more and more embroidery machines arrived. This meant much more could be made, and faster.
26677.m: In the 19th century more and more embroidery was done by machine.

26678.q: Where was St Gallen embroidery mainly sold?
26678.e: The embroidery went to America, England, France and many other countries.
26678.m: St Gallen embroidery was sold all over the world.

26679.q: What position did embroidery hold among Swiss exports around 1910?
26679.e: Around 1910 embroidery ranked as Switzerland’s most important export, even ahead of watches.
26679.m: Around 1910 embroidery ranked as Switzerland’s top export.

26680.q: What did eastern Switzerland produce in large quantities for the whole world around 1900?
26680.e: Tens of thousands of people worked in embroidery around St Gallen. The fine fabrics were sold all over the world.
26680.m: Around 1900 eastern Switzerland was world-famous for its embroidery.

26681.q: Where can you look at old embroidery in St Gallen?
26681.e: The Textile Museum St Gallen shows lace and embroidery from many centuries.
26681.m: The Textile Museum St Gallen shows old embroidery.

26682.q: What was St Gallen embroidery often used for?
26682.e: Fine embroidery and lace decorated dresses, blouses and underwear.

26683.e: Karl Elsener was a cutler and made the famous Swiss Army knife.

26684.q: In which canton was Karl Elsener’s workshop?
26684.e: The workshop stood in Ibach near Schwyz.
26684.m: Karl Elsener worked in the canton of Schwyz.

26685.q: Who did Karl Elsener make knives for from 1891?
26685.e: In 1891 he delivered the first soldier’s knives to the Swiss Army.
26685.m: Karl Elsener made knives for the Swiss Army.

26686.q: What colour is the handle of the typical Swiss Army knife?
26686.e: The typical Swiss Army knife has a red handle with a Swiss cross.
26686.m: The typical Swiss Army knife is red.

26687.q: Who did Karl Elsener name his company Victoria after?
26687.e: His mother’s name was Victoria. Later “inox” for stainless steel was added.
26687.m: The company Victorinox bears the name of Elsener’s mother.

26688.q: What is especially handy about a Swiss Army knife?
a: It has many tools in one
It has an extra long blade
26688.e: Besides blades it often has scissors, a saw, an awl, a screwdriver and a tin opener.
26688.m: A Swiss Army knife has many tools in one.

26689.q: Which symbol is on many Swiss Army knives?
26689.e: On the red handle there is a shield with the Swiss cross.
26689.m: There is a Swiss cross on the Swiss Army knife.

26690.q: In which city was Henry Dunant born?
26690.e: Henry Dunant came into the world in 1828 in this city on Lake Geneva. He worked as a businessman.
26690.m: Henry Dunant was born in Geneva.

26691.q: Which organisation did Henry Dunant help to found?
26691.e: In 1863 Henry Dunant founded the Red Cross together with other men. It helps injured people and people in need.
26691.m: Henry Dunant is the founder of the Red Cross.

26692.q: Who did Henry Dunant help after the Battle of Solferino?
26692.e: In 1859, after a battle, Dunant saw thousands of wounded soldiers. He helped them together with women from the village.
26692.m: Henry Dunant helped wounded soldiers at Solferino.

26693.e: Solferino is a village in northern Italy. A big battle took place there in 1859.

26694.q: What does the Red Cross symbol look like?
26694.e: The symbol is a red cross on a white background. It is the Swiss flag with the colours swapped.
26694.m: The Red Cross uses the colours of the Swiss flag, swapped round.

26695.q: Which famous prize did Henry Dunant receive in 1901?
26695.e: The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded for the first time in 1901. Henry Dunant was one of the two winners.
26695.m: Henry Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize.

26696.q: In which Appenzell village did Henry Dunant spend his last years?
26696.e: In old age Dunant lived in Heiden in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden and died there in 1910. Today Heiden has a Dunant museum.

26697.q: What is the Red Cross called in many Muslim countries?
26697.e: In many countries with a Muslim population, the organisation is called the Red Crescent. It belongs to the same movement as the Red Cross.
26697.m: The Red Crescent is part of the Red Cross movement.

26698.q: Why is World Red Cross Day celebrated on 8 May?
26698.e: Henry Dunant was born on 8 May 1828. That is why 8 May is World Red Cross Day.
26698.m: World Red Cross Day falls on Dunant’s birthday.

26699.q: Which famous children’s book did Johanna Spyri write?
26699.e: Johanna Spyri wrote the story of Heidi. The book is known all over the world.
26699.m: Johanna Spyri is the author of Heidi.

26700.q: What is Heidi’s grandfather called in the book?
26700.e: Heidi’s grandfather lives alone in a hut high up on the mountain pasture. People call him the Alm-Uncle.
26700.m: Heidi’s grandfather is called the Alm-Uncle.

26701.q: What is the name of the goatherd who is Heidi’s friend?
26701.e: Peter looks after the village goats up on the mountain pasture. Heidi often goes up with him.
26701.m: Heidi’s friend Peter is a goatherd.

26702.q: To which city does Heidi have to move to live with Clara?
26702.e: Heidi is taken to Frankfurt in Germany. There she is meant to keep the sick girl Clara company.
26702.m: Heidi lives with Clara in Frankfurt for a while.

26703.q: Why does Clara use a wheelchair in the book “Heidi”?
26703.e: Clara is ill and cannot walk. Up on the mountain she learns to walk again with Heidi’s help.
26703.m: Clara learns to walk again on the mountain.

26704.q: What is the name of the strict housekeeper in Frankfurt in the book “Heidi”?
26704.e: Miss Rottenmeier runs the household for Clara’s family. She is very strict with Heidi.
26704.m: Miss Rottenmeier is the strict housekeeper.

26705.q: In which canton is the story of Heidi set?
26705.e: Heidi lives above Maienfeld in the canton of Grisons. Today there is a Heidi Village there.

26706.q: What are the names of Grandfather’s two goats in the book “Heidi”?
26706.e: The Alm-Uncle has two goats called Schwänli and Bärli. Heidi loves them very much.
26706.m: The Alm-Uncle’s goats are called Schwänli and Bärli.

26707.q: What does Heidi bring for the goatherd’s blind grandmother?
26707.e: The grandmother finds it hard to eat hard bread. So in the city Heidi collects soft rolls for her.
26707.m: Heidi saves soft rolls for Peter’s grandmother.

26708.q: What job did Albert Anker do?
26708.e: Albert Anker was a Swiss painter. He lived from 1831 to 1910.
26708.m: Albert Anker was a famous painter.

26709.q: In which village in the canton of Bern did the painter Albert Anker live?
26709.e: Albert Anker was born in Ins in the Bernese Seeland and lived there. You can visit his house today.

26710.q: Who did Albert Anker especially like to paint?
26710.e: Anker often painted children playing, learning or sleeping. These pictures are very popular.

26711.q: Where are many of Albert Anker’s paintings set?
26711.e: Anker showed simple life in the countryside. You see classrooms, farmhouse parlours and old people in the village.

26712.q: What can you see in Albert Anker’s painting “The School Walk”?
26712.e: In the picture a school class goes on an outing with the teacher. The children walk along a path.
26712.m: The School Walk shows children on an outing.

26713.q: What did Albert Anker first want to become before he became a painter?
26713.e: Anker was meant to become a pastor and studied at university for it. Then he switched to painting.
26713.m: Albert Anker first wanted to become a pastor.

26714.q: In which big city did Albert Anker learn to paint?
26714.e: Anker studied in Paris with the Swiss painter Charles Gleyre. Later he spent many winters in Paris.
26714.m: Albert Anker learned to paint in Paris.

26715.q: Apart from pictures, what else did Albert Anker paint?
26715.e: Anker painted many designs for ceramic plates. That way he earned extra money.

26716.q: The painter’s name, Anker, is German for “anchor”. What is an anchor?
26716.e: An anchor holds a ship in its place. Albert Anker simply had this word as his family name.
26716.m: An anchor holds a ship in place.

26717.q: What job did Ferdinand Hodler do?
26717.e: Ferdinand Hodler is one of the best-known Swiss painters. He lived from 1853 to 1918.

26718.q: In which city was Ferdinand Hodler born?
26718.e: Hodler came into the world in Bern in 1853. His family were poor.

26719.q: In which city did Ferdinand Hodler live for most of his life?
26719.e: Hodler moved to Geneva as a young man. He painted many pictures there and died there in 1918.

26720.q: What did Ferdinand Hodler often paint?
26720.e: Hodler painted many landscapes with mountains and lakes. He often used clear colours and shapes.
26720.m: Ferdinand Hodler liked painting mountains and lakes.

26721.q: What is the man doing in Hodler’s painting “The Woodcutter”?
a: He is cutting down a tree
26721.e: The woodcutter swings an axe at a tree. The picture is very powerful and well known.
26721.m: The woodcutter chops down a tree with an axe.

26722.q: Which three mountains did Ferdinand Hodler paint together in one picture?
26722.e: Hodler painted the three mountains of the Bernese Oberland above a sea of fog. They stand side by side and can be seen from far away.
26722.m: Hodler painted the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau.

26723.q: By which lake did Ferdinand Hodler learn to paint as a boy, and later paint it again and again?
26723.e: As a boy Hodler learned to paint in Thun. He painted Lake Thun with its mountains again and again.

26724.q: Which Swiss hero with a crossbow did Ferdinand Hodler paint?
26724.e: Hodler painted William Tell as a strong man stepping out of the clouds. Tell carries his crossbow.

26725.e: Gottfried Keller was a Swiss poet and writer. He wrote novels, stories and poems.
26725.m: Gottfried Keller wrote poems and stories.

26726.q: In which city did Gottfried Keller live?
26726.e: Gottfried Keller was born in Zurich in 1819 and also died there in 1890. He played an important part in his city.

26727.q: What is Wenzel’s job in Keller’s story “Clothes Make the Man”?
26727.e: Wenzel is a poor tailor in a fine coat. Because of that, people mistake him for someone else.
26727.m: In “Clothes Make the Man”, Wenzel is a tailor.

26728.q: Who do people think Wenzel is in “Clothes Make the Man”?
26728.e: Because of his fine clothes, everyone believes Wenzel is a noble count. That is how the mix-up begins.
26728.m: Because of his clothes, people take Wenzel for a count.

26729.q: Which colour is in the title of Gottfried Keller’s great novel?
26729.e: The novel is called “Green Henry”. Henry wears green clothes sewn from his father’s clothes.

26730.q: What did Gottfried Keller first want to become as a young man?
26730.e: Keller went to Munich to become a painter. Only later did he become a famous poet.
26730.m: Gottfried Keller first wanted to become a painter.

26731.q: What is the made-up little Swiss town in Gottfried Keller’s stories “The People of ...”?
26731.e: Keller invented the little town of Seldwyla. Many of his funny and sad stories take place there.
26731.m: Keller’s made-up little town is called Seldwyla.

26732.q: Which official post did Gottfried Keller hold for many years?
26732.e: From 1861 to 1876 Keller served as First State Secretary. So he also wrote a lot in his job.
26732.m: Gottfried Keller served as State Secretary in Zurich.

26733.q: What job did Jeremias Gotthelf do?
26733.e: Gotthelf preached every Sunday in his village church. On the side he wrote many books.
26733.m: Jeremias Gotthelf worked as a pastor.

26734.q: What is Jeremias Gotthelf’s real name?
26734.e: Jeremias Gotthelf is a pen name. In real life he had the name Albert Bitzius.
26734.m: Jeremias Gotthelf’s real name is Albert Bitzius.

26735.q: In which area did Jeremias Gotthelf live as a pastor?
26735.e: Gotthelf served as pastor in a village in this area. It is known for its hills and farms.

26736.q: Who did Jeremias Gotthelf mainly write about?
26736.e: Gotthelf told of the lives of farmers in his area. He showed their work, their worries and their faith.
26736.m: Gotthelf wrote about the lives of farmers.

26737.q: Which spooky story did Jeremias Gotthelf write?
a: The Rider on the White Horse
26737.e: In “The Black Spider” a giant spider brings disaster to a village. It is a well-known scary story.

26738.q: Where does Uli work in Gotthelf’s book “Uli the Farmhand”?
26738.e: Uli works as a farmhand on a farm. In the book he learns to be hard-working and thrifty.
26738.m: In the book Uli is a farmhand on a farm.

26739.q: In which little town was Jeremias Gotthelf born?
26739.e: Gotthelf came into the world in Murten in 1797. His father served there as pastor.

26740.q: What did Jeremias Gotthelf mainly write about in his novels?
26740.e: Gotthelf served as pastor in Lützelflüh in the Emmental. His first novel, “The Peasant’s Mirror”, came out in 1837.
26740.m: Gotthelf wrote about farm life in the Emmental.

26741.q: In which canton is Lützelflüh, where Gotthelf served as pastor?
26741.e: Lützelflüh is a village in the canton of Bern. Today it has a Gotthelf centre.
26741.m: Lützelflüh is in the canton of Bern.

26742.q: Marie Heim-Vögtlin was the first woman in Switzerland to have which job?
26742.e: Marie Heim-Vögtlin became the first Swiss woman doctor. At that time almost only men could become doctors.
26742.m: Marie Heim-Vögtlin became the first Swiss woman doctor.

26743.q: At which university did Marie Heim-Vögtlin study?
26743.e: She began her studies there in 1868. Zurich accepted women early on.

26744.e: If you want to become a doctor, you have to study medicine. Marie Heim-Vögtlin did this as the first Swiss woman.

26745.q: Which canton did Marie Heim-Vögtlin come from?
26745.e: Marie Vögtlin was born in 1845 in Bözen in the canton of Aargau. Her father served there as pastor.

26746.q: What job did Albert Heim, Marie Heim-Vögtlin’s husband, do?
26746.e: Albert Heim studied mountains and rocks. He became a well-known geologist in Zurich.
26746.m: Albert Heim worked as a geologist.

26747.q: Which patients did Marie Heim-Vögtlin especially treat?
26747.e: In her practice she mainly helped women and children. She also helped at births.
26747.m: Marie Heim-Vögtlin mainly helped women and children.

26748.q: What did Marie Heim-Vögtlin found with other women in 1901?
a: A nursing school with a hospital
26748.e: She helped to found the Swiss Nursing School with a women’s hospital. Women learned nursing there.
26748.m: Marie Heim-Vögtlin helped to found a nursing school.

26749.q: When did Marie Heim-Vögtlin finish her studies as a doctor?
26749.e: She became a Doctor of Medicine in 1874 and then opened her own practice. That was something completely new at the time.
26749.m: Marie Heim-Vögtlin became a doctor in 1874.

26750.q: Emilie Kempin-Spyri was the first woman in Switzerland in which profession?
26750.e: In 1887 Emilie Kempin-Spyri became the first Swiss woman to earn a doctorate in law. She became the first woman lawyer.
26750.m: Emilie Kempin-Spyri became the first Swiss woman lawyer.

26751.e: She studied law. In 1887 she finished with a doctorate.

26752.q: Which famous writer is Emilie Kempin-Spyri’s aunt?
26752.e: Johanna Spyri married Emilie’s uncle. That made her Emilie’s aunt.
26752.m: Johanna Spyri was Emilie Kempin-Spyri’s aunt.

26753.q: Which subject did Emilie Kempin-Spyri study up to a doctorate, as the first Swiss woman to do so?
26753.e: In 1887 in Zurich, Emilie Kempin-Spyri became the first Swiss woman Doctor of Law. Even so, she could not work as a lawyer.
26753.m: Emilie Kempin-Spyri became the first Swiss woman with a doctorate in law.

26754.q: Which big American city did Emilie Kempin-Spyri travel to in order to teach?
26754.e: In New York she taught law to women. There she helped to set up a law school for women.
26754.m: Emilie Kempin-Spyri taught in New York.

26755.q: What did Emilie Kempin-Spyri fight for?
26755.e: She wanted women to have the same rights as men. For this she wrote texts and gave talks.
26755.m: Emilie Kempin-Spyri fought for women’s rights.

26756.q: At which university was Emilie Kempin-Spyri the first woman allowed to teach, in 1891?
26756.e: In 1891 she became a lecturer at the University of Zurich. She became the first woman allowed to teach there.
26756.m: Emilie Kempin-Spyri became the first woman to teach at the University of Zurich.

26757.q: Which court refused in 1887 to let Emilie Kempin-Spyri work as a lawyer?
26757.e: She turned to the highest court in Switzerland. The Federal Supreme Court said no, because it saw equal rights for women as too new.
26757.m: The Federal Supreme Court rejected her case.

26758.q: What job did Le Corbusier do?
26758.e: Le Corbusier planned and built houses, churches and whole parts of cities. He is one of the most famous architects in the world.
26758.m: Le Corbusier worked as an architect.

26759.q: In which Swiss town was Le Corbusier born?
26759.e: Le Corbusier came into the world in 1887 in La Chaux-de-Fonds in the canton of Neuchâtel. The town is known for watches.
26759.m: Le Corbusier came from La Chaux-de-Fonds.

26761.q: Which Swiss banknote showed Le Corbusier?
26761.e: Le Corbusier appeared on the yellow 10-franc note of the eighth series. This series came out from 1995.
26761.m: Le Corbusier appeared on the old 10-franc note.

26762.q: What did Le Corbusier wear on his face in many photos?
26762.e: Le Corbusier almost always wore round, dark glasses. You can recognise him by them in pictures.

26763.q: Which building material did Le Corbusier especially like to use?
26763.e: Le Corbusier built many houses out of concrete. With it he could build smooth walls and large windows.
26763.m: Le Corbusier liked building with concrete.

26764.q: In which country did Le Corbusier build most of his buildings?
26764.e: Le Corbusier lived in Paris for a long time and built a lot in France. Later he became a French citizen.
26764.m: Le Corbusier built mainly in France.

26765.q: Who did Le Corbusier build the small house on Lake Geneva in Corseaux for?
26765.e: He built the small house “Villa Le Lac” for his parents. It stands right on Lake Geneva.
26765.m: Le Corbusier built his parents a house on Lake Geneva.

26766.e: Alberto Giacometti mainly made figures out of bronze. He also painted.

26767.q: What do Alberto Giacometti’s best-known figures look like?
26767.e: Giacometti’s human figures are very tall and very thin. You recognise them straight away.
26767.m: Giacometti’s figures are tall and thin.

26768.q: Which canton did Alberto Giacometti come from?
26768.e: Giacometti was born in 1901 in Borgonovo in the mountains of the Grisons. He is also buried there.
26768.m: Alberto Giacometti came from the Grisons.

26769.q: In which valley did Alberto Giacometti grow up?
26769.e: The Bregaglia is a valley on the border with Italy. People there speak Italian.
26769.m: Giacometti grew up in the Bregaglia.

26770.q: What job did Giovanni Giacometti, Alberto’s father, do?
26770.e: Alberto’s father Giovanni Giacometti became a well-known painter. Alberto learned to draw from him as a child.
26770.m: Alberto’s father worked as a painter.

26771.q: Which Swiss banknote showed Alberto Giacometti?
26771.e: Giacometti appeared on the blue 100-franc note of the eighth series. One of his figures could also be seen on it.
26771.m: Giacometti appeared on the old 100-franc note.
